## Context

`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §7 names the `v1.0.0` row of the release ladder as "stabilize and declare": `1.0` is a promise, so the last release proves it instead of adding capability. On 2026-08-27 no tracker record existed for any §7 item (search of 254 open records for semver, surface, acceptance test, breaking, forward-version, compatibility: zero hits on the §7 work). The row carries seven items; two are already recorded elsewhere (`basicly-tcmy.24` error-path polish, open; `basicly-u2hl.46` scope precedence, closed) and are referenced, not duplicated.

The exit criteria are the §7 exit criteria verbatim: the acceptance test passes on a machine that has never seen this repo; the compatibility policy is published; a surface-breaking commit without a `!` marker fails deterministically; `v1.0.0` is tagged by `basicly release` with both pushes owner-approved.

## Success Criteria

- The five consumer surfaces are enumerated in one machine-readable place and frozen: CLI commands and flags, `basicly.toml` plus the `.basicly-local/` overlay contract, the catalog source schemas, the generated-file contract, and the owned ledger event format.
- A commit that changes a frozen surface without a `!` marker is refused by a deterministic gate (hook and `basicly verify`), with a test that trips it.
- A published compatibility policy states what `1.x` promises for each surface and how a break is announced.
- A fresh consumer repository (git plus a uv-provisioned interpreter, nothing else) installs basicly, runs every gate green, and drives one unit of work to a landed commit; this runs as a test, not as prose.
- The next Python minor is exercised in CI so the `3.14+` floor claim is tested, not asserted (CI edits need explicit owner confirmation; the child names that).
- The two requirements documents are folded into the architecture and deleted, and §3 of the plan is refreshed once; the plan file itself is deleted when the ladder is spent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the frozen-surface manifest when `basicly verify --mode full` runs then a diff to any listed surface in the commit under test without a `!` in the subject fails the `surface-freeze` check naming the surface.
- Given a clean machine with git and uv when the acceptance test runs then it installs the packaged basicly into a new repository, every projection gate passes, and one task record advances intake to a landed commit.
- Given `docs/` when the release is cut then a compatibility policy document exists, is linked from the README, and names each of the five surfaces.
- Given `basicly release 1.0.0 --dry-run` when run on main then release-notes, release-fragments and docs-claims are green and the dry run prints the assembled notes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/**`
- `tests/**`
- `.basicly/core/**`
- `.scripts/**`
- `docs/**`
- `README.md`
- `basicly.d/**`
- `changelog.d/**`

acceptance: The repository shall carry one committed machine-readable snapshot at `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` keyed by the five clause names of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` (cli-surface, config-surface, catalog-source-schemas, generated-file-contract, ledger-format), each entry derived from the code that defines it: the argparse tree of `cli._build_parser()` (commands, subcommands, flags), the accepted section and key names of `config.CONFIG_SCHEMA` for basicly.toml and basicly.local.toml, the `$id` and `required`/`properties` of `.basicly/core/schemas/{fragment,skill,agent}.schema.json`, the generated-manifest `version` and the projected output set, and `events.KNOWN_KINDS`, `events.KNOWN_FIELDS`, `events.EVENT_FAMILY` and `events.LOG_GLOB` from `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`.
When `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_freeze.py --check` runs on a tree whose derived surfaces equal the committed snapshot, it shall print `surface-freeze: 5 surfaces current` and exit 0.

When a derived surface differs from the committed snapshot, `--check` shall exit 1 and print one line per drifted surface naming the surface clause and the first differing entry (for example `surface-freeze: cli-surface drifted: +flag verify --frobnicate`), and the same finding shall appear in `basicly verify --mode fast` and `--mode full` as a failing check named `surface-freeze` declared in `basicly.d/basicly-kosxhm.1.toml`.

When `--fix` runs, it shall rewrite `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` from the code and print `surface-freeze: snapshot regenerated`; the verify entry shall declare no `fix_command`, so the fast set never regenerates the freeze on the author's behalf.

The snapshot shall be byte-identical when generated on Linux, macOS and Windows (sorted keys, LF, posix paths), asserted in `tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py` together with a positive control that a mutated parser produces a drift naming `cli-surface`.

The `ledger-format` clause of `integrity._CONSUMER_SURFACES` shall also claim `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`, and `tests/test_integrity.py`'s exactly-one-level property shall still hold over every tracked file.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_freeze.py --check` prints `surface-freeze: 5 surfaces current` and exits 0; then `uv run pytest tests/test_check_surface_freeze.py tests/test_integrity.py -q` collects more than 0 tests and passes; expected reading: the check line names exactly five surfaces and the pytest summary line ends in `passed`.
tasks.title: freeze the five consumer surfaces in one committed snapshot and refuse an unregenerated drift

acceptance: When `basicly verify --mode full` runs and any commit in the range under test (the lane's `merge-base(base_branch, HEAD)..HEAD`, or `HEAD~1..HEAD` on the base branch itself) changes `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` while its subject carries no `!` before the colon, the check named `surface-breaking-marker` (declared in `basicly.d/basicly-kosxhm.2.toml`, mode `full`) shall exit 1 and print one line per offending commit naming the short sha, the subject and every surface clause whose snapshot entry that commit changed.

When every commit in the range that changes the snapshot carries a `!` marker, or no commit in the range changes it, the check shall print `surface-breaking-marker: <n> commits checked, 0 unmarked surface changes` and exit 0.
If the range cannot be derived (no base branch, shallow clone with no merge base), the check shall exit 1 naming what it could not read rather than pass vacuously.
The `pre-push` hook shall refuse such a push by running the same check, because pre-push runs the `full` mode (`.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`); no hook source is edited.
`tests/test_check_surface_breaking_marker.py` shall build a temporary repository, commit a snapshot change with and without `!`, and assert the two verdicts and the surface named in the refusal.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_surface_breaking_marker.py --range HEAD~1..HEAD` on a commit that touches `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` with subject `chore: probe` exits 1 naming that sha and `cli-surface`; the same commit with subject `chore!: probe` exits 0 printing `1 commits checked, 0 unmarked surface changes`. `uv run pytest tests/test_check_surface_breaking_marker.py -q` collects more than 0 tests and passes.
tasks.title: refuse a commit that moves the frozen surface snapshot without a breaking marker

acceptance: The repository shall carry `docs/compatibility.md` stating, for each of the five surfaces, what a `1.x` release promises (what may be added, what may not change without a major) and how a break is announced: a `!` commit subject, a `changelog.d/<id>.removed.md` or `.changed.md` fragment, and a major version bump by `basicly release`.

The list of the five surfaces in `docs/compatibility.md` shall be a `docs-claims` generated block rendered from `.scripts/frozen_surfaces.json` (registered in `.scripts/docs_claims.py`), so `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check` fails when the snapshot's surface set and the published list disagree.
README.md's Documentation section shall link `docs/compatibility.md`, and `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check` and `npx --no-install markdownlint-cli2` shall stay green on the new page.
The document register at `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §9 shall carry a row for `compatibility.md` marked consumer-facing with the precondition `never deleted while 1.x is supported`.
The tutorial's install pins in `docs/tutorial/first-loop.md` shall not be edited by this child; it edits only the four files above and its changelog fragment.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check` prints a summary whose generated-block count is one higher than today's `4 generated blocks current` and exits 0; `rg -n 'compatibility.md' README.md` prints exactly one line; `rg -c 'cli-surface|config-surface|catalog-source-schemas|generated-file-contract|ledger-format' docs/compatibility.md` prints 5 or more.
tasks.title: publish the compatibility policy for the five frozen surfaces and link it from the readme

acceptance: `tests/test_acceptance_fresh_consumer.py` shall build this checkout into a wheel with `uv build --wheel` into a temporary directory, create an empty git repository under `tmp_path` with a scrubbed environment (no PYTHONPATH to this checkout, HOME pointed at an empty directory), and run `uvx --from <wheel> basicly install` there; the test shall be skipped with the reason `uv not on PATH` when `shutil.which('uv')` is None and shall never import `basicly` from this checkout inside the consumer.

When the install has run, every projection gate (`basicly check`, `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots`, `basicly agents-check`, `basicly hooks-check`, `basicly permissions-check`) and `basicly verify --mode full` invoked through the same `uvx --from <wheel>` pin shall exit 0 in the consumer, and the test shall assert each exit code and the absence of `.beads/` and of any file referencing this checkout's path.

When the consumer files one task record with `basicly tracker write -- create ...`, drives it with `basicly loop run <id> --work-type task --runner manual`, re-runs each reprinted `--confirm <code>` command parsed from the previous output, commits on the harness branch, and runs the loop to landing, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <lane-branch> main` shall succeed and `basicly loop status <id>` shall report the record landed; the sequence shall follow `docs/tutorial/first-loop.md` steps 3 to 7, so the tutorial is executed rather than described.

The test shall assert that the installed skills live at project scope under `.claude/skills/` and that a same-named skill placed under the scrubbed `HOME/.claude/skills/` is left untouched by install and uninstall, which is the behaviour `basicly-u2hl.46` recorded; it shall not claim any shadowing detection, because none exists in `src/basicly/`.

While the test runs under the repository's `pytest` verify check (`-n 4`), it shall write nothing outside `tmp_path` and shall not depend on network beyond what `uvx` needs to resolve the wheel's declared dependencies.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_acceptance_fresh_consumer.py -q -rs` collects more than 0 tests and the summary line reads `passed` (not `skipped`) on a machine with `uv` on PATH; expected reading: one test, taking under two minutes, no `skipped` in the summary.
tasks.title: prove a fresh consumer with only git and uv installs the packaged basicly and lands one unit of work

acceptance: This child edits `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` (and nothing else under `.github/`) plus CONTRIBUTING.md; editing a CI workflow requires explicit owner confirmation before the first write, and the lane shall stop with a `needs-input.json` naming that confirmation if it has not been granted.

When the `quality-gates` workflow runs on `main` or a pull request, it shall include one additional job that installs the next Python minor (`3.15`, pre-release if no final exists, via `astral-sh/setup-uv` with `python-version: 3.15` or `uv python install 3.15` and `UV_PYTHON=3.15`) on `ubuntu-latest`, runs `uv sync`, `uv run python -m basicly.cli catalog lint` and `uv run python .basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`, and reports its own result under a job name containing `3.15`.
The new job shall carry the same 30-minute `timeout-minutes` as the existing matrix job and `continue-on-error: false`, so a red result on the forward interpreter blocks like every other gate.

If `3.15` is not installable by uv on the runner, the job shall fail naming the interpreter it could not install rather than silently fall back to 3.14; the lane shall verify this by reading the job log of one real run, not by reasoning about the YAML.

CONTRIBUTING.md (lines stating `Python 3.14+` and `CI runs the same set`) shall name the two interpreters CI exercises (3.14 and the next minor), so the contributor-facing claim matches the workflow; `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, `uv.lock` and README.md shall not be edited by this child.
tasks.demonstration: `gh run list --workflow quality-gates.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId,conclusion` then `gh run view <databaseId>` lists a job whose name contains `3.15` with conclusion `success`; locally, `uv run --python 3.15 python -c 'import sys, basicly; print(sys.version_info[:2], basicly.__version__)'` prints `(3, 15) 0.9.0` when uv can provision 3.15.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This child edits `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` (and nothing else under `.github/`) plus CONTRIBUTING.md; editing a CI workflow requires explicit owner confirmation before the first write, and the lane shall stop with a `needs-input.json` naming that confirmation if it has not been granted.
- When the `quality-gates` workflow runs on `main` or a pull request, it shall include one additional job that installs the next Python minor (`3.15`, pre-release if no final exists, via `astral-sh/setup-uv` with `python-version: 3.15` or `uv python install 3.15` and `UV_PYTHON=3.15`) on `ubuntu-latest`, runs `uv sync`, `uv run python -m basicly.cli catalog lint` and `uv run python .basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`, and reports its own result under a job name containing `3.15`.
- The new job shall carry the same 30-minute `timeout-minutes` as the existing matrix job and `continue-on-error: false`, so a red result on the forward interpreter blocks like every other gate.
- If `3.15` is not installable by uv on the runner, the job shall fail naming the interpreter it could not install rather than silently fall back to 3.14; the lane shall verify this by reading the job log of one real run, not by reasoning about the YAML.
- CONTRIBUTING.md (lines stating `Python 3.14+` and `CI runs the same set`) shall name the two interpreters CI exercises (3.14 and the next minor), so the contributor-facing claim matches the workflow; `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, `uv.lock` and README.md shall not be edited by this child.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `8000000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `gh run list --workflow quality-gates.yml --branch main --limit 1 --json databaseId,conclusion` then `gh run view <databaseId>` lists a job whose name contains `3.15` with conclusion `success`; locally, `uv run --python 3.15 python -c 'import sys, basicly; print(sys.version_info[:2], basicly.__version__)'` prints `(3, 15) 0.9.0` when uv can provision 3.15.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"One of the biggest issues with agentic development in the terminal alone is that human has no idea what is going on and when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried under."*

Reproduced in 27 seconds on 2026-09-05 while dispatching a real lane.

## Measured

| time | fact |
| --- | --- |
| 17:02:56Z | `loop supervise basicly-lc2bd3v --label cockpit-first --max-passes 1 --detach` |
| 17:02:5xZ | log: `adopted: basicly-vowpbar (open) -> basicly-vowpbar on harness/basicly-vowpbar [live]` |
| 17:02:5xZ | log: `stopped: --max-passes 1 reached after 1 pass(es), 1 child(ren) still open` |
| 17:03:0xZ | `basicly worktree list`: `basicly-vowpbar: harness/basicly-vowpbar (base main)` |
| 17:03:23Z | the served board: `RUNNING NOW no pass is running - 238 record(s) are ready to start` |

A worktree was on disk, its `worktree:` binding was in the ledger, and the board said nothing was running.

## Cause

`board_facts.py:610-622`:

```python
lanes=(
    lane_facts(repo_root, session.root_issue, phase_map, lane_label=lane_label)
    if in_flight and session is not None
    else ()
    if board_serve.live_holder(repo_root) is None
    else None
)
```

`()` means *"no pass is running"*, and it is chosen whenever no process holds the lock. So visibility is keyed to a **live supervisor process**, not to work in flight. The moment the supervisor exits - because it finished its rounds, because a terminal closed, or because it crashed - every lane it provisioned disappears from the board while its worktree stays on disk.

The second channel does not catch it either. `board_regions.claimed` filters `status == "in_progress"`, and a provisioned child is still `open`, so it is in neither population.

## Not basicly-9guj21

That record is about work with **no** `worktree:` binding at all - a host subagent or a background shell job. This record is the opposite case: the binding exists, the lane was adopted by name, and it is still invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record carries a live `worktree:` binding and no supervisor holds the lock, THE BOARD SHALL still name it, its branch and its phase.
- THE BOARD SHALL distinguish a lane an agent is inside from a worktree standing open with nobody in it: the second is not a running pass and must not be drawn as one.
- WHERE the lock is held, THE PRESENT behaviour SHALL be unchanged, so a supervised pass still reports its own selector.
- A REGRESSION TEST SHALL provision a binding with no lock and assert the board names it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_claimed.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: dispatch with `--max-passes 1`, let the supervisor exit, and read the worktree on the board

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-r343` fixed the schema scan and could not land without a size waiver. This bead removes that waiver by doing the work the waiver stands in for.

```text
.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py   6,554 frozen, 6,525 used   29 tokens of headroom
the r343 fix adds                829 tokens
now                            7,432 tokens               1.86 times the cap
```

## Why the waiver is not the right end state

`factory-loop.md` section 9.3 states that the first change to a frozen file **under 8,000 tokens** must bring it under the cap, not merely reduce it. This file was 6,554, so the recorded obligation was to extract.

A waiver is for a module that is genuinely cohesive. The `r343` implementer named a real seam in its own report and then waived on cost rather than on cohesion. It said so plainly, which is why this bead exists rather than a silent concession.

## The seam it named

The reference index is a nameable responsibility that does not import back: `_iter_files`, `_read`, `_dotted`, `Index` and `build_index`. It is about a 2,000-token move and it touches every function in the file plus `tests/test_verify.py`.

## Measure before you cut

The two size ratchets pull opposite ways. Extracting code raises the remaining prose share, so an extraction fixes both gates only when the extracted unit's prose share is above its origin's. Measure both with the gates' own scripts before choosing the cut.

## Acceptance

- When the extraction lands, then `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is under the 4,000-token cap.
- When the module-size gate runs, then the waiver count returns to 1 and the waiver comment is gone from the file.
- When `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` is read, then it no longer carries a module-size waiver delta.
- When the dead-code gate runs before and after, then it reports the same finding count.
- When both size gates run, then neither baseline is raised.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- a new module under `.scripts/`
- `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` reports the same count as before the split, and `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports one waiver rather than two.

legitimate case `python-guidelines` names, a module whose payload is provenance — and land the origin

payload.description:
## Context

Root cause of the only CI red this session (run 30168113819, macos-latest, three tests): the StallWatchdog tests asserted a timing outcome after a fixed time.sleep, so passing depended on how fast the host scheduled a background thread. Green on ubuntu and windows, red on macos. The failure did not reproduce locally even under twelve CPU spinners, so the constant could not have been tuned with any confidence - the shape of the test was wrong, not the number in it.

The test-discipline skill already carries two sections paid for by earlier sessions (Set up the condition the code actually reads, and A seam is not duplication). It has nothing about timing.

Proposed section, authored as a general rule with no Python or basicly specifics: 'Wait for the condition, not for a duration.' A test that sleeps then asserts encodes an assumption about host speed, and the assumption is invisible until the slowest runner in the matrix disagrees. Poll the condition with a generous timeout instead, so the test asserts what it means (the thing happened) rather than when it happened. Pair it with the prohibition's alternative: if the assertion really is about elapsed time, measure it with a monotonic clock and assert a bound, never a sleep-then-check. Include the corollary that a fixed sleep long enough for the slowest CI runner is far too slow for a laptop suite, so tuning the constant trades one failure mode for another.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the test-discipline skill when it is projected then it carries a section teaching wait-for-the-condition over fixed sleeps with the monotonic-bound alternative, authored as a general rule with no language-specific or repo-specific detail, and the catalog lint and skills-check gates pass

## Context

Found 2026-07-31 by the basicly-axqe lane and measured 2026-08-01 before filing.

`schema.ValidationError.__str__` renders `f"{self.path}: {self.message}"`, and every call site
passes an absolute path. So a load-time validation failure prints a machine-specific absolute path
on a user-facing surface, while `catalog_lint`'s own violations print a repo-relative one.

## Measured

Both lines below come from ONE `basicly catalog lint` run over a scratch consumer repo, with the
same bad value (`technologies: [notatechnology]`) placed in an overlay source and in a core source.
The first line is the load-time `ValidationError`, the second is `_check_technology_vocabulary`:

    <abs><redacted:posix-absolute-path>: unknown technologies: ...
    .basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml: unknown technologies: ...

Same finding, same run, two path styles - so the inconsistency is visible to a single reader, and
the absolute form is the one that leaks a home directory or a username into anything pasted into an
issue or a CI log. The repo rule is that no user- or machine-specific path is ever emitted, and
there is a `tracker-path-scan` hook enforcing the same principle for the tracker export; nothing
enforces it for lint output.

## Not in scope

The same probe measured the OTHER asymmetry the axqe lane reported - that
`_check_technology_vocabulary` is core-only for agent sources. That is NOT a defect: an overlay
source with a bad technology value is already rejected (rc=1) by `schema.validate_technologies` at
load time. The core-only walk is redundant on that axis, which is exactly why the core case reports
the finding twice and the overlay case once. No bead is owed for it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/schema.py`
- `tests/test_schema.py`

payload.description:
## Context

The two size ratchets are the largest recurring tax on this repository's own lanes, and no epic owns them. Four open records name `.scripts/check_module_size.py` or `.scripts/check_comment_density.py` and none had a parent, so the system that keeps inflicting the cost was invisible as a system.

## Measured

`uv run python .scripts/headroom.py`: **178 of 447 tracked modules are within 615 tokens or 1.0 point of a bound.** 20 sit at exactly zero token headroom, 46 at exactly zero prose headroom, and 2 at both. **17 modules are frozen in both tables** - the genuinely double-bound set.

`TIGHT_TOKENS = 615` is not a preference. It is the median of 44 real `module_size` rebaseline declarations, so it is this repository's measured cost of **one ordinary unit's edit to one module**. About 40% of the tree is therefore one ordinary edit away from refusing the next one.

## The trap is arithmetic, not judgement

Removing a unit from a module raises that module's prose share whenever the unit is **prose-lighter than the parent**. So a cut that satisfies `module-size` breaks `comment-density`. Measured over **3,588 real top-level definitions in the 68 frozen oversized modules: only 34.4% are prose-heavier than their parent** and therefore satisfy both at once. Two in three natural extractions make the module worse.

`.scripts/check_comment_density.py` already knows: `prose_tokens` raises rather than returning zero precisely because an extraction is safe only when the extracted unit is prose-heavier.

## What it has cost, measured

`basicly-kr7t` is a documented total lane loss. It built the named extraction, measured it against both ratchets, and reverted - after enumerating **all 8.4 million subsets** of the file's 26 natural blocks with the gates' own measurement functions and finding that **225,756 satisfy both ratchets and not one is a nameable responsibility.** The refusal margin was 28 prose tokens, 112 characters.

`basicly-u2hl.1` committed, rebased, and did not land, blocked on module-size.

Three of four lanes in the 2026-08-22 pass independently reported the ratchets as systemic and spent budget on them rather than on their task. One of them, `basicly-0hxck3`, could not take the nameable cut at all: every one of the 116 modules under `src/basicly/` is named in `.importlinter`, so a new module needs a line in a file another unlanded lane declared, and it shipped a `cost()` waiver instead.

A median lane is 6.76M tokens and about six dollars.

## What this epic is not

It is **not** a proposal to raise either cap. Both are grounded. 4,000 is `read_cost.SCOPE_FILE_READ_CAP`, the point where an agent stops reading a file whole and starts reading selectively - it is a working-set constant shared with the loop's budgeter, so moving it changes lane sizing everywhere. 50.0% was measured over 280 modules on 2026-08-12, median 36.3% and p75 51.2%, chosen to refuse the worst quartile. Nor is it a licence to hand-edit a frozen table; a loosening delta is refused and should stay refused.

The goal is that a lane meeting a bound can find the right answer in one step, and that the tree stops accumulating modules with no seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane meets a bound, THE GUIDANCE AND THE GATE'S OWN REMEDY SHALL together name a route that its own parser accepts, and the route SHALL be reachable without editing a file another lane declares.
- WHEN a split is proposed, ITS EFFECT ON BOTH GATES SHALL be computable before the cut is made, rather than discovered by making it.
- WHEN the tree grows, THE COUNT OF MODULES WITHIN ONE ORDINARY EDIT OF A BOUND SHALL fall rather than rise, and that count SHALL be reported.
- WHERE a module genuinely has no seam, TAKING THE WAIVER SHALL cost one step and SHALL NOT require a lane to enumerate its subsets to discover that.

payload.description:
## Context

Raised by a waiver taken on 2026-09-06, and filed as the record that retires it.

`src/basicly/board_actions.py` was split at the `module-size` gate's own instruction: the endpoint half - spawn, validation, HTTP, audit - moved to `board_action_surface`, leaving a table of six action declarations and the reason for each. The split fixed the size gate and pushed `comment-density` from 50.1% to 54.1%, because what left was code-dense and what stayed is declaration plus rationale.

Measured across the move: 125 lines left the module and only 31 of them were prose.

## The question

**Is a prose ratio the right measure for a module that is mostly a declaration?** The gate exists to catch narration - a comment restating the statement below it - and it is good at that. A table of six argv builders is different in kind: each entry is two or three lines of data and the reason it is that argv rather than another, which is exactly what the repo's rules ask code to carry.

Three ways this could go, and the record exists to choose one rather than to leave a waiver standing:

1. **The measure is right and the module is wrong.** Then the reasons belong somewhere else - the architecture document, or one block comment rather than eight docstrings - and the waiver retires by moving them.
2. **The measure needs a population discriminator.** A module whose top-level statements are overwhelmingly a literal declaration is a different population from a module of functions, and the cap could read it as such. This is the shape `a-ratchet-needs-a-population-discriminator` describes.
3. **The split was wrong.** Unlikely - the size gate demanded it and the seam was real - but stated so it is refutable.

## What was tried before waiving, so it is not repeated

The module docstring's four paragraphs were split by subject: three described the confirm-code friction, the redaction property and the HTTP trust boundary, all of which had moved to `board_action_surface`, so they moved with the code they describe. Five function docstrings were then rewritten shorter by hand. One mechanical compression pass was attempted, produced sentences truncated mid-thought, and was reverted - a rationale cut to fit a ratio is worse than the ratio.

The figure did not move off 54.1% across all of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE WAIVER on `src/basicly/board_actions.py` SHALL be removed in the same change that resolves this record, whichever of the three ways is chosen.
- WHERE the answer is that the measure needs a discriminator, THAT DISCRIMINATOR SHALL be bound to something the producer of the module writes, not to a name or a path - an absence must not be ambiguous.
- WHERE the answer is that the reasons belong elsewhere, EVERY REASON SHALL survive the move: the count of distinct claims before and after is the check, not the character count.
- A TEST SHALL fail if this waiver outlives the record, so it cannot become a standing exemption.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Working Set

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `50000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run the density gate with the waiver removed and read either a passing module or a discriminator that says why a declaration table is a different population.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a commit run from a linked worktree when the harness prose is projected then it states that provisioning already wires the shared hooks dir and that overriding it with a relative core-hooksPath resolves to nothing and silently skips every hook
payload.description:
## Context

Session retro (basicly-kjc5.9). A commit run from a loop worktree with `git -c core.hooksPath=.git/hooks commit` passed with no hook output: a linked worktree has `.git` as a *file*, so the relative path resolves to a directory that does not exist and git skips every hook silently - pre-commit, commit-msg, and the beads gate all bypassed without a word. The next amend without the override caught a subject the gate rejects, proving the first commit had been ungated.

Root cause: nothing in the harness prose says the shared hooks dir is already wired by provisioning and must not be overridden. The worktree-isolation skill documents hook provisioning but not this failure mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the worktree-isolation skill when an agent commits from a loop worktree then the skill states that hooks are already wired to the shared dir and that overriding core.hooksPath there silently disables every gate with the projection gates green

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/worktree-isolation/**`

## Finding
Reported by the handily session on 2026-11-18: in a fresh clone of handily, the PreToolUse and SessionStart hooks refused every Read and Bash call with: repository-local Lefthook runtime is missing. Run the repository's pinned basicly command with hooks-build --runtime-only. The agent cannot run that repair, because Bash is refused too. After a manual hooks-build, hooks-check reported drift because the global basicly was older than the pin.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05, restating a requirement they say they have given many times: *"the requirement was also to make the board interactive or a cockpit or a control panel where we can see and control the flow of work. Cool thing would be to be able to easily start, stop work, descope and so on."*

And the reason, in their words: *"One of the biggest issues with agentic development in the terminal alone is that human has no idea what is going on and when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried under. Terminal is fast and no one scrolls up, having multiple terminals does not help."*

And the test they set: *"if you as an agent look at the board, and only have access to the board, would you be able to see what is going on? what work is available, what work can start, is in progress? start work, stop work, inspect work (the info written in the record in a structured way)? descope work, scope work?"*

Explicitly **not** in scope: *"it is not about creating new records - that we can do via terminal. it is about work loop transparency and control."*

And the standing instruction: *"the board, even if it is a byproduct of basicly, it is essential and should grow with the basicly."*

## The gap, measured

Taken against the served board at 127.0.0.1:8788 on 2026-09-05, and against the snapshot it renders.

| the owner's question | answered today | by what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what work is available | partly | `NEXT UP` draws 3 of 234 ready |
| what can start now | yes | `THE QUEUE`: 262 needs nothing, 24 waits on one, 8 waits on a chain |
| what is in progress | yes | `RUNNING NOW` and `CLAIMED, NO LANE` |
| what is blocked, and by what | yes | `THE QUEUE` names the top blockers and the longest chain |
| **inspect one record** | **no** | `units[]` carries `id, phase, priority, ready, status, title, type` and no body |
| **start work** | **no** | no action offers `loop run` or `supervise` |
| **stop work** | partly | `lane-kill` is in `ACTIONS`, but only reachable when an ask prefills it |
| **descope / scope** | **no** | no action changes status or priority |
| when will it be done | no | `basicly-hymq99` and `basicly-w6vbw61` |

So four of nine. The two channels that are missing are **inspect** and **control**, and they are missing for different reasons.

## The seam already exists

`board_actions.ACTIONS` is a closed table of three argv builders handed to the installed CLI as a subprocess. Its docstring states the design: *"The board is a renderer with a keyboard."* `.importlinter`'s `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` contract holds because the board never reads the tracker; it runs `basicly`.

That is the answer to inspect as well as control. A record's body does not have to enter the snapshot - 294 bodies would be a snapshot nobody can serve. The board runs `basicly tracker show <id>` the same way it runs `basicly policy checkpoint`, and renders what comes back. No contract moves.

`board_asks.pending` already prefills a row per implementable offer. What is missing is a surface for an action that no *ask* proposes - a ready record has no ask, so today nothing offers to start it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an agent has the board and nothing else, IT SHALL be able to answer all nine questions in the table above, and a test SHALL enumerate them so the board cannot drift back into a report.
- WHERE a verb changes the flow of work, THE BOARD SHALL offer it on the row it applies to, not only where an ask happens to prefill it.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT gain the ability to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.
- `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` SHALL still hold: every new capability is an argv handed to the installed CLI.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- children decompose this; each is a leaf a lane can build

Scope correction 2026-09-05. The inspect half of this epic was already filed as basicly-62h3x9 on 2026-08-28, as a feature under the same parent, with a superset of the criteria I wrote. basicly-vowpbar is closed as its duplicate. This epic keeps the four verbs nothing else covers: fiow1sr start, x1h1dl5 stop, arxhshr defer and reactivate, udunil8 the nine-question gate. Establishing that took two probes - the first searched titles for a board word beside a verb word and missed 62h3x9 outright, because its title carries neither start nor stop nor action. The second listed every one of the 62 records whose title names the board or the wall and read the 20 still open. An empty probe is not evidence of absence.

## Redefined by the owner, 2026-09-06 — the cockpit is a development environment

> *"the board is the human instrument for implementation of new features. the human will set

> environment for a human, where he sees what is going on and can react on it."*

**This supersedes the wall framing.** The board was built as a glance surface read from across
a room, and every design decision followed from that: cap the lists, prefer counts to members,
draw a diagram rather than a backlog. Those were right for a wall and are wrong for a cockpit.
`basicly-a68ggd` is the clearest case - it is closed, and its title is *"the loop region shows

re-closes `a68ggd`'s finding on top of it.

terminal*. The cockpit is where a human **views and controls the implementation**. So the
cockpit does not need record creation - it needs seeing and reacting.

**Two surfaces, not one page:**

1. **The loop** - what is happening now, as a kanban of phase columns in the shape Linear and
   Jira use, where each phase names its members and a member is reachable.
2. **The backlog** - what is planned, ordered, with the controls to shape it.

priority, and dependency."* The board leads with ids in most regions today.

*"4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."* Shared
branch, shared worktrees. `basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped worktree visibility, which is one agent's
answer to "who is inside a lane"; it says nothing about which *session* holds what, whether two
are about to collide, or what a fifth terminal joining should be told.

**Priority:** the owner has made visualization number one, on the ground that the cockpit is
*"the 1st thing a user will see when starting basicly after installation in their repo"*.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an agent has the board and nothing else, IT SHALL be able to answer all nine questions in the table above, and a test SHALL enumerate them so the board cannot drift back into a report.
- WHERE a verb changes the flow of work, THE BOARD SHALL offer it on the row it applies to, not only where an ask happens to prefill it.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT gain the ability to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.
- `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` SHALL still hold: every new capability is an argv handed to the installed CLI.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- children decompose this; each is a leaf a lane can build

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, listing the cockpit actions an enterprise board must carry: *"parking, prioritizing, changing scope"*.

Measured 2026-09-06 against `board_actions.ACTIONS`, which is the closed table of everything the board can run: it holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. Parking and resuming already answer *descope* and *scope*. **Nothing changes a priority.**

That leaves the ranked lists the board draws - `NEXT UP`, `THE QUEUE`, the ready set - read-only. An operator who can see that the wrong thing is ranked first must leave the board to move it, which is the exact loss the cockpit exists to stop.

## The verb already exists

`basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` is the priority write, and it is the same shape the existing park and resume actions use - an argv handed to the installed CLI, never a tracker read. So `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` is unaffected.

## No confirm code, and the reason

The rule `record-park` states: a checkpoint carries a code because it is the human gate the anti-autopilot rule protects. A priority spends nothing, starts nothing, and is undone by setting it back. It is the same class as park, so it takes no code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator submits a priority for a record, THE BOARD SHALL run `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` through the installed CLI and show that command's own exit status and output.
- WHERE the board draws a record in a ranked list, IT SHALL offer the priority change on that record's own row, not only where an ask prefills it.
- THE ACTION SHALL refuse a value the tracker will refuse, before the subprocess runs, and say which values are allowed.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action's own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.
- A TEST SHALL assert the argv reaches the CLI and changes the record, not that the argv has the right shape - the shape-only test is why `basicly-fiow1sr` shipped an argv that started nothing.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_action_wire.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: open a record page on a served board, submit a new priority, and read the record's rank move in the next fold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator submits a priority for a record, THE BOARD SHALL run `basicly tracker write -- update <id> -p <n>` through the installed CLI and show that command's own exit status and output.
- WHERE the board draws a record in a ranked list, IT SHALL offer the priority change on that record's own row, not only where an ask prefills it.
- THE ACTION SHALL refuse a value the tracker will refuse, before the subprocess runs, and say which values are allowed.
- THE PRINTED COMMAND SHALL be built through the action's own `build`, so the line a reader copies cannot diverge from the argv the button runs.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a lane is claimed or anything is parked, I want the wall to still show me what to work on next, so I can pick the next record without leaving the cockpit for the terminal.

## Steps to Reproduce

Render the wall at the size the owner reads it and look at the region, rather than at a test:

```
uv run basicly board --out wall.html --width 1440 --height 900
```

Observed in the screenshot: `NEXT UP - +246 MORE READY` heads a large empty box. Zero rows are drawn. The parked strip and one claimed row are both present below it.

Driven directly against the real snapshot, the mechanism is the `reserved` argument:

| reserved px | rows drawn | the header still claims |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 3 | +243 more ready |
| 200 | 0 | +246 more ready |
| 400 | 0 | +246 more ready |
| 600 | 0 | +246 more ready |

`board_render` passes `acts_reserve + claimed_reserve + parked_reserve + QUEUE_PX`, so any claimed row or parked strip pushes reserved past 200 and the region empties.

Expected: the region draws at least one row whenever the set is non-empty, or it draws nothing and reserves nothing. A box that reserves height and states a count while showing no rows is the worst of the three.

## Cause

`next_up` takes `slots = fits if wide else min(READY_SLOTS, fits)` and then `slots = max(slots // 2, slots - len(set(names[:slots])))`. The floor protects against feature headings eating slots, but `max(0 // 2, ...)` is 0, so it cannot protect against `ready_capacity` returning 0. `ready_capacity(900, 1440, 0)` is 6 and every reserve above ~200px takes it to 0.

This is NOT caused by basicly-lc2bd3v.9, which changed only that region's `note` line - `git diff` over `board_regions.py` for that record touches nothing else. It is the other half of basicly-zj36jf0, which measured the same region overflowing its viewport by 152px.

## Why no test caught it

5465 tests pass on the commit that renders this. Every one of them asserts a count, a note or a row shape against a fixture whose reserve is 0. Nothing renders the wall at a stated size with a claimed lane present and asserts that the region a reader looks at has rows in it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the ready set is non-empty, THE READY REGION SHALL draw at least one row whatever the reserved height, so a reader is never shown a count with no rows.
- WHERE the region can draw no row at all, IT SHALL reserve no height and SHALL say that the wall is too short, rather than drawing an empty box.
- THE HEADER COUNT SHALL agree with the rows drawn: a region showing N rows of M ready SHALL NOT report M as more-than-drawn when it drew none.
- A TEST SHALL render the wall at 1440x900 with a claimed lane and a parked strip present, and assert the ready region contains at least one record id.
- A TEST SHALL drive `next_up` across the reserve range 0 to 600 px and assert the row count never reaches zero while the ready set is non-empty.
- THE REGION SHALL keep the viewport bound it already honours, so closing this SHALL NOT reopen the 152px overflow basicly-zj36jf0 measures.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render the wall at 1440x900 with a lane claimed, screenshot it, and read rows in the NEXT UP region

payload.description:
## Trigger

When I read the board and an inner component sits flush against the box that contains it, I want every component to take its spacing from one scale, so I can read a region as a group of things instead of as one run-together block.

## Steps to Reproduce

Owner, 2026-09-08, reading the served wall: *"there is not margins or padding, so in some components right now on the board the inner component is glued to the outer component as there is no space between them -> one of many design issues for which we already may have stories."*

Counted over the wall template on 2026-09-08:

| template | padding | margin | gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board_page.html.j2` | 16 | 21 | 29 |
| `board_record.html.j2` | 10 | 9 | 1 |
| `board_kanban.html.j2` | 6 | 4 | 6 |
| `board_backlog.html.j2` | 4 | 5 | 2 |

The wall's 16 padding declarations carry **12 distinct values**, none of them from a scale:

```
9px 12px 10px · 8px · 7px 0 1px · 5px 9px 7px · 5px 10px · 3px 12px
3px 0 · 2px 9px · 2px 5px · 1px 4px · 1px 0 1px 7px · 1px 0
```

Expected: a spacing value on the board is a step on one scale, so a component nested in another cannot end up with none.

## Cause

Every spacing value is decided at the site that needs it, and a site that nobody looked at got zero. Twelve independent decisions is not a design; it is twelve. Nothing fails when a thirteenth is added, and nothing fails when one is omitted.

## Relation to the bootstrap record

This is the defect that argues for basicly-lywzp71 rather than a competing approach to it. Bootstrap ships a spacing scale and utility classes, so closing this by applying that scale is one job with lywzp71's vendoring, while closing it by hand-tuning twelve values into thirteen is the state that produced the observation. Read lywzp71 before starting here, and prefer closing both together.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE BOARD SHALL take every padding, margin and gap value from one declared scale, and a value outside that scale SHALL NOT appear in a template.
- WHERE a component is nested inside another, THE INNER COMPONENT SHALL carry a non-zero inset from its container on every side that has a visible border.
- A GATE SHALL fail naming any board template that declares a spacing value the scale does not contain, so a thirteenth ad hoc value cannot land silently.
- THE SCALE SHALL be stated in one place that the templates read, so changing a step is one edit rather than sixteen.
- A SCREENSHOT at 1440x900 SHALL be taken and read before this is closed, because the counted declarations are the symptom and the rendered gap is the requirement.
- CLOSING THIS SHALL NOT reopen basicly-zj36jf0 or basicly-lc2bd3v.10: added inset costs height, and both of those are regions already short of it.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_kanban.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `.scripts/check_board_spacing.py`
- `tests/test_check_board_spacing.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-lywzp71`
- demonstration: render the wall at 1440x900, screenshot it, and read the inset on a nested component that has none today

## Context

Found by looking at the rendered page of `basicly-62h3x9` on 2026-09-06, minutes after it merged, against the owner's own method: screenshot it and say what a human sees without reading the code.

Two defects, both in what the page omits rather than in what it draws.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`
2. Open `<redacted:posix-absolute-path>`'s record page for an epic, for example `record/basicly-k6tpep.html`.

Observed: `THE TREE` lists fourteen children as bare ids - `basicly-2n5dfe`, `basicly-9guj21`, `basicly-a8jy77` and eleven more - with no titles. And no section anywhere carries the record's description.

Expected: a reader can tell what each child is, and can read what the record says.

## Why each one matters

**Bare ids.** The owner has stated this as a standing requirement: a person cannot read an id, and a record must be named with its title. The board's own ready list already prints `id + title` on every row, so the record page is the one surface that regressed against a rule the rest of the page keeps. `BLOCKED BY` and `BLOCKING` have it too.

**No description.** The owner's words when this surface was asked for: *"inspect work (the info written in the record in a structured way)"*. The page today shows metadata *about* a record and never what the record says, so the question that opened the page is the one thing it cannot answer.

The description was deliberately left out of `basicly-62h3x9` when its data path was decided on 2026-09-06, on the argument that `basicly-lc2bd3v` makes about bodies: 297 of them would be a snapshot nobody can serve. That argument is still true for *every* body at once, and it does not apply to *one*. A record page is one record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the record page prints another record's id - in the tree, in blocked by, or in blocking - IT SHALL print that record's title beside the id, and the id SHALL remain the link.
- WHEN a record page is opened, IT SHALL render that record's description as markdown, so the headings the Definition of Ready requires read as headings.
- WHERE the description would take the page past what one snapshot can carry for every record at once, THE PRODUCER SHALL carry each body on that record's own page rather than in the shared document, so the wall's snapshot does not grow by 297 bodies.
- WHEN a record has no description, THE PAGE SHALL say so as an absence, never as an empty section.
- A TEST SHALL assert a title appears beside an id in each of the three link sections, and SHALL fail if any of them prints a bare id.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_record_page.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_record.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_record_page.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`, open `record/basicly-k6tpep.html`, and read every child's title beside its id and the epic's own description on the page.

Built in the base checkout on 2026-09-07, landed at the commit that names this record. Owner priority: they read a record page mid-session and could see no description and no acceptance criteria, and said so - "how should i then use this to drive test-driven development ... I as human, if that was my backlog i wouldnt even know where to start."

Both defects fixed.

Titles beside ids. The parent line and the three link lists went through one `named()` macro, so four sites cannot become four spellings of the rule. The context carries the titles map the wall already builds from `units[]` - no new data.

The description. Rendered as markdown by `board_render.markdown`, a Jinja filter using markdown-it-py with `html=False`. That flag is the security boundary and not a formatting choice: every other producer string on the page is autoescaped, so a renderer that passed embedded markup through would be the one hole in that. A test asserts `<script>` in a body reaches the page escaped.

The data path. `board_bodies.bodies()` folds the ledger once and returns 1249 descriptions keyed by id. Not a snapshot section: 304 bodies is a document nobody can serve, which is this epic's argument, and it holds for every body at once and not for one. `harness-board/v1` is unchanged. `board_snapshot` was the first home and crossed the 4000-token cap, so the read moved to its own module along a nameable responsibility rather than taking a waiver.

Measured. `basicly board --out` writes 307 record pages in 3.2s total - one fold, not 307, asserted through the seam rather than by timing. The epic `basicly-k6tpep` renders six body headings and names all fourteen children by title. `check_render_overflow` reports nothing clipped and nothing overlapped.

Four gates fired on the new module and each was fixed rather than waived: `module-size` on `board_snapshot` and on `test_board_record_page` (both split), `comment-density` on the new module (docstring cut to the two facts the code cannot state), `test-naming` (a test file named after it), `noqa-debt` (the first S704 in this tree, declared in `basicly.d/` with its reason), and `docs-claims` (the layering block regenerated for the new tier).

One thing found and not fixed here: `.scripts/check_test_naming.py` cites `§9.4` three times and no document in this tree defines it. I stated the rule in words in my own line rather than carry an unresolvable pointer. Worth a record.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, reading the board's alarm band: *"i have no idea what these 3 waiting on the person want from me"*.

The band was drawing `1 HOUR - 3 WAITING ON A PERSON`, one record's name, an engine sentence, and `+2 more waiting`. Everything a person needed to act was either absent, truncated, or wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Land three records so each sits at `verify` with its ship checkpoint unapproved.
2. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read the band.

Observed: one ask named, two hidden behind a count, the offered command cut off as `do:...`, and the question reading `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it`.

## The five defects, in the order they cost a person time

**1. The offered command does not do the job.** Each ask carries `actions[].offer = "basicly loop advance <id>"`. Run against a merged record it prints:

```
[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval
```

What actually ships it is `basicly loop run <id> --root <epic-with-a-grant>`, which the board never mentions. **This is the serious one**: an operator surface that prints a command which stops one step short teaches the operator that the board is wrong, and the other four defects are cosmetic beside it.

**2. Only one ask of three is named.** The other two exist only as `+2 more waiting`. A person cannot act on a count.

**3. The offer is truncated.** The band has the exact argv and cuts it at the right edge.

**4. The question is written for the engine.** `verify is cleared and nothing is scheduled to advance it` describes a scheduler state. A person needs the consequence: this merged, advancing it closes the record and tears the worktree down.

**5. There is no advance action.** `board_actions.ACTIONS` holds `loop-answer`, `checkpoint-approve`, `record-park`, `record-resume` and `lane-kill`. `advance` is the most common thing waiting on a human on this board and it is not offered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE an ask carries an `offer`, THE BOARD SHALL print a command that reaches the state the ask is waiting for, verified by running it, and SHALL NOT print one that stops at an unapproved checkpoint.
- WHEN more than one ask is pending, THE BOARD SHALL name every waiting record and its own command, rather than naming one and counting the rest.
- THE OFFERED COMMAND SHALL be rendered without truncation, wrapping instead of clipping where the column is narrow.
- THE ASK SHALL state the consequence of acting in a person's terms alongside the engine's own wording, never instead of it.
- WHERE an ask's kind is `advance`, THE BOARD SHALL offer it as an action on that ask's row, through an argv handed to the installed CLI like every other action.
- A TEST SHALL run each offered argv against a fixture at the state the ask describes and assert it reaches the next state, so an offer that stops short fails rather than renders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_advance.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_advance.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: leave three records waiting at ship, read the board, and run each command it prints - each reaches ship without a second command the board did not name.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, reading a wall whose lower half was empty: *"maybe we can have a way to click somewhere on the board and see the full backlog list so we can plan what to do next better?"*

## Measured

Taken from the board rendered at 1600x1400 on 2026-09-06:

| what the wall draws | what exists |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT UP` lists **4** records, then `+233 MORE READY` | 237 ready |
| `THE QUEUE` gives four counts and three blocker ids | 1,251 records, 298 active, 57 blocked |
| blank page below `NEXT UP` | roughly 600 of 1400 pixels, 43% of the wall |

So the one surface an operator plans from shows 1.7% of the ready set, and the space to show more is already there and empty.

## Why a page rather than a bigger region

The wall is a glance surface read from across a room and it is right to cap a list. A plan is a different act: it is done at a desk, it wants every record, and it wants sorting and grouping the wall must not spend space on. `basicly-62h3x9` already established the shape - `board --out` writes 297 record pages beside the wall and `board serve` answers `<redacted:posix-absolute-path><id>` - so one more page costs no new mechanism.

This is **not** `basicly-c9crxu`. That record is about the wall's own ready column not reading the viewport, and it stays true whatever this one does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator follows the backlog link from the wall, THEY SHALL reach a page listing every open record, not a capped sample.
- EACH ROW SHALL carry the record's id as a link to its page, its title, its priority, its status, its phase and whether it is ready - the fields a person sorts on when choosing what to do next.
- THE PAGE SHALL group by feature, naming the parent each record belongs to, and SHALL name the records that belong to no feature rather than dropping them.
- THE PAGE SHALL let a reader see the blocked set and what blocks each member, because a plan that ignores blockers plans work nobody can start.
- WHERE the wall prints a count it caps - the ready set, the queue, the blocked set - THAT COUNT SHALL be the link to this page, so the way in is where the reader already looks.
- THE PAGE SHALL be written by `board --out` beside the record pages and served by `board serve`, from the snapshot, so `consumer-reads-only-the-snapshot` still holds.
- A TEST SHALL assert the page lists every record `units` carries, so a cap cannot be reintroduced silently.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`, follow the ready count from the wall, and count the rows on the page against `basicly tracker stats`.

The page is /backlog on the server and backlog.html beside a --out board, reached from three capped counts on the wall: the NEXT UP overflow, the backlog strip label and the queue label. Three sites named before the edit and three replaced.

The demonstration the plan names, run: 'basicly board --out' wrote backlog.html at 153 KB with 304 id cells. The snapshot carries 304 units. 'basicly tracker stats' gives open 297 + blocked 2 + deferred 4 + in_progress 1 = 304. Three paths, one number, and the header's 241 ready equals the tracker's 241.

Two findings worth the record.

1. The header first said '34 blocked' while 63 records are not ready. Those are two populations: only 34 carry a blocks edge, so 29 are unstartable for a reason no edge names - a parent not decomposed, a DoR unmet. One word for both would tell a planner that 29 records are startable when they are not. The header now reports 'not ready' and 'waits on a named blocker' as separate figures, and a test pins the distinction.

2. My first blocker count read 37 and the page read 34. The page was right: three blocks edges have a 'from' that units no longer lists, and board_record._edges drops those as a debt already paid. My looser probe was the faulty instrument. Direction matters here and is easy to invert - 'from' is the BLOCKED record and 'to' is the blocker, which is the opposite of how the JSON reads at a glance, so board_backlog imports board_record's constants and states the direction in a docstring rather than deriving a second answer.

check_render_overflow found what nothing else could: under table-layout fixed a 'width: 1%' column is literally 1% and its content painted over the title by 66 to 80px on three rows. Auto layout fixed it; the page now reports nothing clipped and nothing overlapped at 1920x1080.

Ten tests, including one against the live socket and one that counts rendered id cells against units so a cap cannot be reintroduced in the template - an assertion against groups() alone would not have caught that.

Also filed while here: basicly-vs0m8oj, a pre-existing flake in test_supervise_board where a freshness assertion compares two wall-clock reads and went negative by 0.88s under the full-suite load.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06, on what a backlog surface must do beyond listing:

> *"get inspired by jira, linear, clickup, asana, youtrack... we need a better dependency visualization system than those tools provide. then I could open a backlog and prioritize it, and during prioritization the dependencies would always be considered, so constraints would be set in place. Example: if moving an item from 5th position to the 1st, and that item has an item dependent on item on 4th position, that means that 4th item must be done before 5th and the 5th cannot be placed before it. The system would in this case visualize what items are connected and in which order when one is selected, and will prohibit sorting the backlog in a way that breaks dependencies."*

And the framing: *"adapt these concepts to the agentic-first development, which also humans, if visualized correctly, used."*

## The design question this forces, which must be answered before any code

**This repository has no rank field.** `basicly tracker ready` reports a rank, and it is *computed*, not stored:

```
$ uv run basicly tracker ready --limit 3 --json
{"rank": 1, "record": "basicly-94bk",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 2, "record": "basicly-a3yi",   "score": 3001, ...}
{"rank": 3, "record": "basicly-g5ce75", "score": 3001, ...}
```

`scheduler.ranking()` derives the order from priority, dependent count and id, and `Ranking` carries the sort policy beside the rows *"because a rank recorded without its policy is uninterpretable later"*. Three records tie at 3001 today, so the visible order between them is the tiebreak, not a judgment anybody made.

So a drag to position 1 has nowhere to land. Two honest routes, and this is the decision to take first:

**(a) The drag writes `priority`.** No new state. The engine already reads priority and every consumer inherits the change. But priority is coarse - five buckets, 480 records at P1 - so a drag inside a bucket changes nothing and the item springs back. Honest, and visibly weak.

**(b) The ledger gains a stored rank the scheduler reads ahead of its computed score.** A drag means something exact. It costs a new field, a new event kind, a migration for 1,253 records, and it puts a human's ordering above the engine's - which is either the point or the danger, depending on the owner's answer.

**Do not build until this is chosen.** A drag that appears to work and is silently ignored by the dispatcher is worse than no drag, and it is the exact failure `basicly-fiow1sr` already shipped once: an argv that looked right and started nothing.

## What the research already settled, and nobody has used

Two closed spikes from 2026-09-04 are the reading for this, and both are unactioned:

* `basicly-hnnmk9.6` - dependency-ordered scheduling in established practice. Its load-bearing finding is that **this repo orders lanes on write-scope overlap, not on consumed results** (`decompose.serializes`, an anti/output dependence model), while declared `depends_on` edges are carried separately. So there are *two* orderings, and a backlog that honours only the declared graph will let a human order two items that collide at the merge.
* `basicly-hnnmk9.9` - an inventory of the nine graphs this repository maintains, including the record dependency graph and the file contention graph, and where they do and do not compose.

The owner's constraint rule is a topological one, and the spike names its literature: Kahn 1962, CPM, and GNU make's *order-only prerequisite* - an edge that imposes ordering without implying data flow, which is precisely the shape of a contention edge.

## What the named tools do, and where each stops

| tool | ordering | dependency handling | where it stops for us |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jira | stored `Rank` (LexoRank), drag writes it | blocks/is-blocked-by shown as a badge; ordering is not constrained | a human may rank a blocked item first and nothing objects |
| Linear | stored sort key, drag writes it | blocking relations, and a blocked item is marked | same: the warning is advisory |
| ClickUp / Asana | manual order per list | dependencies with optional date shifting | shifts dates, does not refuse an order |
| YouTrack | saved queries and sort | issue links, `depends on` | sort is a query, not a constraint |

**None of them refuses a reorder.** They warn. The owner is asking for refusal, which is the thing that is actually new here - and it is only defensible because our graph is machine-consumed: an order a dispatcher will really execute is worth constraining, where a human backlog order is advisory anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator selects a record in the backlog, THE PAGE SHALL draw that record's dependency neighbourhood - what it waits on, what waits on it, and the order those imply - and SHALL distinguish a declared `blocks` edge from a contention edge derived from overlapping scope.
- WHEN an operator moves a record above one it depends on, THE PAGE SHALL refuse the move and SHALL name the chain that forbids it, rather than accepting it with a warning.
- WHERE a move is legal, THE PAGE SHALL apply it through an argv handed to the installed CLI, and the resulting order SHALL be the order `basicly tracker ready` then reports - or the move SHALL be refused as unrepresentable.
- THE PAGE SHALL NOT invent an ordering the engine does not read: a drag whose effect the dispatcher ignores is a lie the operator will act on.
- WHERE two records are unordered by any edge, THE PAGE SHALL say they are unordered rather than implying the list position is a decision.
- A TEST SHALL attempt a dependency-violating move against a fixture and assert it is refused, naming the chain, with a control asserting a legal move is applied.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_backlog.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `tests/test_board_backlog.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-lc2bd3v.4`
- demonstration: open the backlog, select a record and read its neighbourhood, then attempt to move a dependent above its blocker and read the refusal naming the chain.

payload.text:
OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07, unblocking this record. A drag writes a STORED RANK FIELD, not a priority bucket.

The ledger gains a rank the scheduler reads before scheduler.ranking computes one; the computed ranking becomes the fallback for records that carry no stored rank, not the answer. The rejected alternative was writing one of five priorities, which fails because 487 records sit at P1 - a drag inside a bucket would spring back and the board would read as broken.

What this implies and was not decided here: the field needs a migration path for 304 active records that have none, an ordering that survives two concurrent writes, and a rule for where a newly created record lands. Those are this record's design work, not further owner questions.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"the loop part: the states have numbers, but are not interactive and i cannot see which items are in classify, intake, decompose, build, and so on - we need interactivity."*

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` and read `THE LOOP`.

Observed: seven boxes carrying a count each - `268 intake`, `2 classify`, `27 decompose`, `1 build`, `0 verify`, `0 validate`, `0 ship`, `954 done`. No box names a record. Nothing is reachable.

Expected: each phase names the records sitting in it, and each is reachable.

## This reverses a closed decision, deliberately

`basicly-a68ggd` is closed and titled *"the loop region shows the whole backlog binned by phase instead of the running pass"*. The region was changed **away** from listing what sits in each phase, because a wall read from across a room should show the pass and not the backlog.

That was right for a wall. The owner has redefined the surface as a development environment a person works at (`basicly-lc2bd3v`), and at a desk the members are the point. **Do not re-close `a68ggd`'s finding on top of this**: its concern - that the running pass must stay legible and not be drowned by 268 intake records - is still true, and is the reason the columns below are capped and ordered rather than dumped.

## The shape, from the tools the owner named

Linear and Jira both draw a column per state with cards in it, a count in the column header, and a card that opens the item. The adaptation here is that our columns are **loop phases**, which are not a workflow a human moves cards between - the engine moves them. So the column is a view, and the actions on a card are the loop's own verbs, not a drag between columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a reader opens the loop surface, EACH PHASE SHALL be a column naming the records in it, with its count in the column header.
- EACH CARD SHALL lead with the record's title, and carry its id, priority and type as secondary - the owner's ordering, not the reverse.
- A CARD SHALL be the link to that record's page, so a phase is a way in and not a dead end.
- WHERE a phase holds more records than the column draws, THE COLUMN SHALL say how many more and SHALL remain readable - `intake` holds 268 and a column that dumps them is the defect `basicly-a68ggd` closed.
- THE COLUMN ORDER SHALL be the loop's own order, so the surface reads left to right as work flows.
- WHERE a record in a column has a live worktree, THE CARD SHALL say so, so a reader can tell a phase a record is parked in from one being worked.
- A TEST SHALL assert every phase the engine defines has a column, so a phase added later cannot be invisible.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_kanban.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_kanban.html.j2`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_board_kanban.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_kanban.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `100000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: open the loop surface and read which records sit in `classify`, `decompose` and `build` by title, then follow one card to its record page.

payload.text:
Built in the base checkout on 2026-09-07 and landed with the tree green. The owner declined a lane: loop preflight reported classify UNAPPROVED blocks provisioning, grant NONE, budget MISSING and a ~23.2M token forecast for one unsizeable lane.

The surface is a second page, not a ninth region: board_kanban.columns over the snapshot, board_kanban.html.j2, served at /loop and /loop.html, and written as loop.html beside a --out board. The wall's loop heading now carries a 'columns' link, or the page would be unreachable from the board that names it.

Each criterion, against the served page at 127.0.0.1:8787 and a 1400x760 screenshot:
- a column per phase naming its records, count in the header - drawn: intake 272, classify 2, decompose 27, build 0, verify 0, validate 0, ship 0
- the title leads, id and priority and type secondary - asserted by position inside one card, not by presence
- the card is the link - the whole card is the anchor, and only for an id the document lists a unit for
- overflow stated and readable - the header reads '12 of 272' as well as the '+N more' line, because the line under the last card is below the fold on a tall column
- the loop's own order - taken from board_loop.PHASES, never a second literal
- a live worktree named on the card - marked, and ordered first so a held record can never be the card the cap drops
- a test that every engine phase has a column - asserted against PHASES itself

Two numbers derived twice: the kanban's per-phase counts equal a hand count over the same snapshot.json, and equal the wall diagram's own digits on the same fetch, so the two surfaces do not contradict each other.

Also found and fixed: test_board_operator_questions probed 'value="lane-start"', an action name that does not exist. That question would have kept xfailing after the control shipped. It now probes record-start with record-park as the positive control, and the board answers 8 of 9 operator questions.

Not done here: an empty column still reserves its full width, and the columns scroll below about 1250px. Neither is in the acceptance.
