payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"think about what will be shown on the cockpit if multiple sessions and agents are working on the same repo in parallel, using same branch and worktrees? One of the use cases I encounter in projects is that 4-5 terminals, each with an open session, are working on the same repository."*

Nothing in the board is designed for this. It is the case the cockpit exists for - the owner's own reason for wanting one is *"when multiple parallel sessions and work is being done, it gets buried"* - and it is the one case no record covers.

## What the board can see today, and what it cannot

`basicly-kqh9dj8` shipped this session and answers **one** question: which records have a worktree, and what git says about each. Measured against the owner's case, that is a third of it.

| the question a fifth terminal arrives with | answerable today |
| --- | --- |
| what worktrees exist and what state is each in | **yes** - `board_unsupervised.lanes` |
| which *session* holds which worktree | no - no session identity is recorded outside a supervisor lock |
| is anybody editing the base checkout right now | no |
| what did the other four sessions just do | partly - the events ticker, unattributed |
| am I about to collide with one of them | no - the contention graph exists and nothing consults it (`basicly-zq9i2m.3`) |
| may I start work on record X | no - `ready` says the tracker permits it, not that a peer is not already on it |

The last row is the sharp one. Two terminals can both read `ready`, both pick the top record, and both start. The tracker's claim is written at provisioning, so the window is small but real, and the loser finds out at the merge queue.

## What identity already exists to build on

* `supervise.read_holder` writes a lock with a `session_id` and a heartbeat - but only a supervisor takes it, which is `basicly-k6tpep.5`'s finding: three capabilities are gated on that lock and a `loop run` operator takes none.
* Every worktree has a name, a branch and a git state, which needs no cooperation from the session that made it.
* The ledger records who claimed a record and when, and it is shared across worktrees by the `redirect` file - so the ledger is the one place all five sessions already meet.

So the honest design direction is **the ledger and the filesystem, not a session registry**: anything requiring five terminals to register themselves will be wrong the moment one crashes, and a heartbeat nobody writes is the stale-lock defect this session already found feeding the header for a whole day.

## What must be decided before building

**Is a session a first-class thing the ledger records, or is it inferred?** Recording it means a new event kind, a heartbeat, and a liveness rule - and a crashed terminal then lies until its heartbeat expires. Inferring it from worktrees and ledger writes means the board can never name a session that has not touched anything, but it also cannot be wrong about one.

Prefer inference until a question is found that inference cannot answer. State the question if one is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN more than one session is working a repository, THE COCKPIT SHALL name each unit of work in flight and which worktree holds it, without requiring any session to register itself.
- WHERE the base checkout is dirty, THE COCKPIT SHALL say so, because a landing refuses on it and the operator who caused it may be at a different terminal.
- WHEN a reader considers starting a record, THE COCKPIT SHALL say whether a peer already holds it, and SHALL distinguish "the tracker permits this" from "nobody else is on it".
- WHERE two units in flight declare overlapping scope, THE COCKPIT SHALL name the overlap before the merge queue does.
- THE COCKPIT SHALL NOT claim a session is alive on the strength of a marker nobody is refreshing: a stale lock fed the header a false run line for a full day on 2026-09-06.
- A TEST SHALL drive two concurrent units against one repository and assert both are named with their holders.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sessions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_sessions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/checkout.py`
- `tests/test_board_sessions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: run two sessions against one checkout, each holding a different record, and read both named with their worktrees on one cockpit.

So the honest design direction is **the ledger and the filesystem, not a session registry**: anything requiring five terminals to register themselves will be wrong the moment one crashes, and a heartbeat nobody writes is the stale-lock defect this session already found feeding the header for a whole day.

## What must be decided before building

**Is a session a first-class thing the ledger records, or is it inferred?** Recording it means a new event kind, a heartbeat, and a liveness rule - and a crashed terminal then lies until its heartbeat expires. Inferring it from worktrees and ledger writes means the board can never name a session that has not touched anything, but it also cannot be wrong about one.

Prefer inference until a question is found that inference cannot answer. State the question if one is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN more than one session is working a repository, THE COCKPIT SHALL name each unit of work in flight and which worktree holds it, without requiring any session to register itself.
- WHERE the base checkout is dirty, THE COCKPIT SHALL say so, because a landing refuses on it and the operator who caused it may be at a different terminal.
- WHEN a reader considers starting a record, THE COCKPIT SHALL say whether a peer already holds it, and SHALL distinguish "the tracker permits this" from "nobody else is on it".
- WHERE two units in flight declare overlapping scope, THE COCKPIT SHALL name the overlap before the merge queue does.
- THE COCKPIT SHALL NOT claim a session is alive on the strength of a marker nobody is refreshing: a stale lock fed the header a false run line for a full day on 2026-09-06.
- A TEST SHALL drive two concurrent units against one repository and assert both are named with their holders.

- `src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sessions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`

Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a lane's phase changes between beats, I want the board to mark that change from a phase stamp, so I can tell a working lane from a wedged one.

## Context

`basicly-a68ggd` split the loop region into a pass row over `lanes[]` and a backlog census over `units[]`, and added a `moved` mark so a reader can tell a working lane from a wedged one.

The mark is taken from `lanes[].state_since`, which is the only movement stamp the `harness-board/v1` contract declares. That field stamps the lane's **state** - `running`, `landing`, `waits-to-land` - and not its **phase**. So the mark answers "this lane did something within the beat", which is a proxy for the acceptance criterion the parent record actually wrote:

> WHEN a unit has moved phase since the previous beat, THAT MOVEMENT SHALL be visible, because a still picture of positions cannot distinguish working from wedged.

## Why the consumer cannot derive it

Two other sources were examined and both refused:

- `events[]` carries the transition, but only inside `text`, as this producer's own string (`id=... phase=ship`). `board_footer.events` joins event fields verbatim and parses none of them, and `board_render`'s own contract is that a foreign producer must render. Parsing `text` would be the first producer coupling in the consumer.
- A consumer-held previous snapshot would work, but `board_render.context` is a pure function of one document by design - "Passed rather than read so a page is a function of its inputs".

The producer knows when a unit changed phase. The consumer cannot.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_loop.py`
- `tests/test_board_loop.py`
- `tests/fixtures/board/wall-v1.json`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass, let one lane cross a phase boundary, render the board and read the mark against the supervisor's own reported transition.
Why merged: Board lane rows continue without the dispatcher (src/basicly/board_unsupervised.py:90 lanes()), so the premise holds. A single optional snapshot field and one mark.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-06: *"the real titles of features and tasks are more important than IDs. IDs should be there but focus is on titles, description, priority, and dependency."*

This is the fourth session in which a version of it has been said, and it is already a saved rule from an earlier one: *a person cannot read an id, so report the id and the title together.* The board keeps doing the opposite in specific places, and each has been fixed as its own defect - `basicly-a8jy77` for the header, `basicly-lc2bd3v.2` for the record page. Fixing sites one at a time is why it keeps coming back.

## Measured

The wall rendered at 1600x1250 on 2026-09-06 prints **23 record ids in its body, 22 of them unique**. The rows that carry a title alongside are the ready list and the lane cards. The rows that do not:

- `PARKED  P4 basicly-0jiq intake  P3 basicly-3iaw0x build  P2 basicly-kjc5.49 intake  P2 basicly-vkh0.4 intake`
- `THE QUEUE ... unblocks most  basicly-uz3m68.1 4  basicly-7bur 3  basicly-vkh0.42.6 3`
- `longest  basicly-uz3m68.5 -> basicly-uz3m68.4 -> basicly-uz3m68.3 -> ...`
- `EVENTS  basicly-e1c4pct  2026-09-06T16:47:58Z  harness-cost  id=basicly-e1c4pct#cost`
- the header's `RUN` line, when it draws

Five regions, one rule, and no gate. A reader is asked to hold 22 opaque strings.

## Why a gate rather than a sixth fix

`basicly-m8cdnv1` - *"every header and footer line earns its place or is cut"* - is **closed**, and the owner has raised the header twice since. A review that passes and a requirement that keeps failing means the review was of the wrong thing. What survives is a check the page has to satisfy on every render, not a judgment made once.

The gate is cheap because the fact is already there: `units[]` carries a title for every record the board draws, so a region printing a bare id is not missing data, it is choosing not to draw it.

## The exception the gate must allow

A **chain** - `a -> b -> c -> d` - cannot carry four titles and stay one line. That region's job is the shape, not the members. So the rule is not "never print a bare id"; it is "a region that names a record as a thing a reader acts on must name it by title", and a region that draws a shape declares itself as such.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE the board names a record as a thing a reader acts on, IT SHALL draw that record's title, and the id SHALL be present as the address rather than as the name.
- WHERE a region draws a shape rather than members - the dependency chain is the case - IT SHALL declare itself exempt in one named list, so the exemption is enumerable rather than implicit.
- A TEST SHALL render the page and fail on any record id outside that exempt list which is not accompanied by its title, naming the region, so a sixth site cannot be added silently.
- THE TITLE SHALL be clipped rather than dropped where a column is narrow, and the untruncated title SHALL remain available on the row.
- WHERE a title is absent from the snapshot, THE ID SHALL stand alone and the absence SHALL read as an absence, never as a record with no name.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_titles.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `tests/test_board_titles.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: render the wall and read every named record by its title, then add a bare id to a region and watch the gate name that region.

Built in the base checkout on 2026-09-07, landed at 0c2cdc8c.

Measured before the fix, on the live fold: 13 bare ids over three regions - the parked strip (4), the queue's unblocks-most list (3) and the events ticker (1), plus 4 chain nodes and 1 probe artefact.

The gate is tests/test_board_titles.py. It renders the wall, strips tags before scanning so an href is never counted as a printed name, matches ids against the document's own set rather than by shape, and fails naming the region. Four assertions: the gate itself, a positive control that watches it catch a bare id, the exemption list pinned to exactly ('chain',), and a check that no id the board draws exceeds board_graph.ID_MAX - latent today, since the longest id here is 18 characters against a 24 bound, and the title lookup is keyed on the id a region printed so a clipped one would find nothing in silence.

board_graph.SHAPE_ELEMENTS is the declared exemption, in product code rather than in the test, so the claim 'this element draws a shape' is reviewable. Only the chain is in it.

Three template sites now draw the title with the id as the address, all reading the titles map board_regions.unit_titles already supplied - no second answer built. The parked row copies the claimed row's idiom one region up, which already did this correctly.

Two things the count-before-replace rule caught. The parked pattern matched two sites and I had named one; the second was the claimed row, which already drew its title, so the script refused and wrote nothing rather than editing a correct site. And check_render_overflow found an 11x20px overlap of the id over the title on two ready rows - pre-existing, reproduced on a render taken before this change - because overflow hidden does not reliably clip a td and an 18-character id at 17px needs 173px of a 158px column. Taken out of the id's font size rather than the title's width, on this record's own principle.

Demonstration run, as the plan names it: removed the title from the parked strip and the gate failed with "region 'ready' names ['basicly-parked1'] with no title". Restored from a copy taken first.

Not fixed here: the events ticker's title only shows where the event's issue is still in units. A ticker line naming a closed record keeps the bare id, which is correct - there is no title to draw and the absence reads as one.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the dispatch gate refuses a record the board has just offered me a start control for, I want the board to tell me which records can actually be built and what each of the others still owes, so I can write the missing trigger on the record I am about to work instead of discovering the refusal one record at a time.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run on `b94ceff9`, the commit that added the trigger gate:

```
uv run basicly tracker ready | grep -c 'basicly-'
```

Observed: **245** records offered as ready. Then fold the same 245 ids through the gate that now governs a dispatch:

```
uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; from basicly import tracker, invest; ..."
```

Observed: **1** of the 245 can enter BUILD - `basicly-q1ve1fn`. The other 244 are refused for a missing `## Trigger`. A positive control ran first: the one record known to satisfy the gate is present in the passing set, so the 1 is a measurement and not an empty probe.

Expected: the cockpit reports a number an operator can act on. A start control drawn on a record the gate will refuse is a control that cannot work.

## Cause

`board_record.startable` reads `unit["ready"]`, which is the tracker's dependency walk and says nothing about the Definition of Ready. `basicly-q1ve1fn` made the DoR strictly stronger without teaching the ready signal about it, so the two disagree by a factor of 245. This is the same class of fault as a board fact keyed on the supervisor lock: the label says one thing and the field means another.

## What must not happen

`board_sections.units` sits below `invest` in the layer contract and must stay there, so it cannot compute this verdict. It receives it, exactly as `phase` and `ready` already arrive from `phases` and `ready` and from nowhere else. And only the missing section *names* may cross the wire - a description on a unit row is the 132.5x regression that module exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the snapshot producer emits a unit row, THE PRODUCER SHALL record what that record owes the Definition of Ready as a bounded list of section names, and SHALL NOT put any record body on the wire.
- THE UNITS BUILDER SHALL receive the verdict as a parameter and SHALL NOT derive it, so the layer contract holds and an absent verdict renders as absent rather than as satisfied.
- WHERE a record owes any required section, THE BOARD SHALL NOT draw a start control for it.
- THE READY LISTING SHALL keep its existing rank order and SHALL name, on each row it cannot start, the section that record owes.
- THE BOARD SHALL report the count that can actually be dispatched alongside the count the dependency walk calls ready, so the two numbers are never presented as one.
- A TEST SHALL assert a record that satisfies every dependency but owes a trigger is not startable.
- A TEST SHALL assert a unit row carries the owed section names and carries no description or acceptance body.
- A TEST SHALL assert an absent verdict leaves the row unmarked rather than startable, so a producer that could not compute it fails closed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `src/basicly/board_record.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_backlog.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_record_page.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: serve the board, read the ready region, and confirm it names one startable record and the owed section on the rest, then check that no start control is drawn on a refused row

Codex has **no glob- or pattern-based instruction scoping** — no `applyTo`, no `paths:` frontmatter,
no `globs` field, in `AGENTS.md` discovery, the config reference, `SKILL.md` frontmatter, or the
customization overview. Directory placement is the only scoping axis. Codex *does* support separate
instruction files (nested `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`),
repo-checked-in skills at `.agents/skills/`, project subagents at `.codex/agents/*.toml`, and project
sandbox rules at `.codex/rules/`. So the mechanism our inlining rests on is the **glob-vs-directory
type mismatch**, exactly as §7.4 says — not any absence of separate files.

### The defects to fix

1. **Two surviving lines assert the rationale that `2d04834` (basicly-joj, 2026-07-15) retired**, and
   they contradict `docs/architecture/architecture.md:653-666` in the same file:
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` — "inlines scoped fragments (codex can't path-scope)"
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:507` — "scoped fragments inlined because it has no
     path-scoping mechanism"
2. **A stronger justification is unrecorded.** Nested `AGENTS.md` is loaded only along the path from
   project root **down to the cwd** — "Codex stops searching once it reaches your current directory".
   A file at `src/foo/AGENTS.md` is therefore **not loaded at all** when codex runs from the repo
   root. Per-directory offload would not merely lose glob fidelity; in the normal case it would not
   load. This strengthens the `[Deferred]` §11.3 offload decision and should be recorded next to it.
   (Exception worth noting: codex code review on GitHub does walk changed files, so that surface
   behaves differently from the CLI.)
3. **Stale cap figure.** `architecture.md:625` says a "shared soft cap of 8,000 chars" and
   `.basicly/core/targets/codex.yaml:4` says "Higher than claude/copilot (8000)", but both YAMLs set
   **9000** (raised in `e70e4db`, basicly-c5to). Also stale in `docs/archive/foundry-spike.md:307,343`.
4. **Stale doc URLs.** `developers.openai.com/codex/*` now 308-redirects to `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`
   and page paths moved (`<redacted:posix-absolute-path>` -> `<redacted:posix-absolute-path>`). Any
   citation of the old path still resolves but is stale. `project_doc_max_bytes` is still 32 KiB and
   is configurable.
5. **Corrected measurements** (the cap counts characters via `len(content)` at `cli.py:311-317`; the
   figures previously carried were bytes):

   | Surface | chars | cap | headroom |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `AGENTS.md` | 10775 | 12000 | 1225 |
   | `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | 7894 | 9000 | 1106 |
   | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | 8026 | 9000 | 974 |

   A scoped fragment costs **~1500 chars (measured 1462 and 1614)**, to `AGENTS.md` only — not the
   "~1600" carried before. So: **copilot is tightest by absolute headroom**; `AGENTS.md` is the
   binding constraint **for the path-scoped tier specifically**, and the **next** scoped fragment
   already overflows its cap (1225 < ~1500) rather than "two more" as previously recorded. Correct
   this wherever it appears, including `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:143`.
6. **Record the naming collision.** Codex's own "Rules" feature is a sandbox command-execution policy
   (`.codex/rules/`, Starlark `prefix_rule(pattern=...)`), unrelated to per-file instructions. Reading
   that page and concluding codex has no instruction rules is the exact trap the owner hit, so the
   distinction is worth one line wherever we describe the codex surface.
7. **Note that file-based custom prompts are deprecated** in favour of skills and are user-scope only
   (`~/.codex/prompts`), so they cannot ship in a repo — relevant if a codex command tier is ever
   proposed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` and `:507`.
2. Read `:653-666` of the same file.
3. Observed: `:496`/`:507` say codex has no path-scoping mechanism, while `:653-666` documents that it
   does (root->leaf concat, nearest wins, `AGENTS.override.md`). The authoritative doc contradicts
   itself, and a reader acting on §4.4 reaches a conclusion the repo retired on 2026-07-15. Expected:
   one consistent rationale — the glob-vs-directory mismatch, plus the root->cwd loading limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture doc and the catalog when the codex steering surface is described then the rationale is the glob-vs-directory mismatch plus the root-to-cwd loading limit with no surviving claim that codex cannot path-scope, the cap figure reads 9000 everywhere, the surface table gives characters not bytes with copilot as the tightest always-on surface, and the per-scoped-fragment cost reads about 1500 with the next fragment overflowing AGENTS.md

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a validator is told to judge a change against the requirement that asked for it, I want that requirement stored on the record as a typed field, so I can validate against a written standard instead of inferring one from prose.

## Requirements

R1. A person reading a closed record can see what intended use the change was validated against, without reading the implementation.
R2. A validator dispatched on a record with no stated intended use is refused rather than asked to guess.
R3. The word `requirements` on a record means the intended use of ISO 9000:2015 3.8.13, never the specification that acceptance criteria hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a caller runs `tracker write -- update <id> --requirements "<text>"`, then the value is stored as the record's `requirements` payload field. [check: `tests/test_tracker_write.py`]
- When `tracker show <id>` prints a record carrying the field, then `requirements` appears in its `fields` map. [check: `tests/test_tracker_write.py`]
- When the engine dispatches the validator for a record whose `requirements` field is empty, then the advance is refused and the refusal names the missing field. [check: `tests/test_loop_validate.py`]
- When an existing record carries no `requirements` field, then reading it succeeds and the field reads as absent rather than as an empty string. [check: `tests/test_tracker.py`]

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_write.py -q`

## Design notes

Architecture section 32.11 and D-50. `tracker_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS` gains the flag; the field joins the payload the same way `acceptance_criteria` already does. Measured 2026-09-13: 0 of 1,347 created events carry this field or a `## Requirements` heading, against a positive control of 761 carrying `## Acceptance Criteria`.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the quality gate fragment states the check step then it names the command that runs every gate and the pass line to confirm, so a hand-picked subset cannot be reported as the gate.
payload.description:
## Context

Session 2026-08-14, and this is a user-visible mistake rather than a near miss: I reported "all
gates green" before committing `basicly-ejdm.2`, then the commit was **refused**. What I had run
was `pytest` plus five checker scripts I picked by name. What I had not run was the gate, which
then failed on `pyright` and `projection-skills`.

The `quality-gate` fragment says: *"Run the repo's checks on anything touched, re-run after the
final edit"*, and *"Point at gates, don't restate them."*

## Root cause, and it is in the wording

"The repo's checks" is a **set an agent has to assemble**, and an agent that has just run five
checkers has evidence it assembled it correctly. There is no moment at which a hand-picked subset
announces that it is a subset - it looks exactly like the whole.

The repo already has the one command: `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` runs all 20 and prints
`checks passed: 20/20`. Nothing in the guidance names it, so the fragment describes an outcome
where it could name a command - which is the inversion of section 3.1, the rule that guidance
points at the enforcement rather than restating it.

## Proposed change, for a human to apply

Amend the `quality-gate` fragment so the check step **names the command** rather than the set:
run the repo's own gate runner, and confirm the pass line it prints. The count in that line is
what makes a subset visible - `18/20` cannot be misread as green, while five green scripts can.

D25 forbids an agent amending the catalog, so this is filed rather than applied.

## The second half, which the wording cannot fix

I also reported the result before running the gate. The fragment already carries
*"Confirm success from the explicit pass/fail summary line; truncated output hides failures"* -
that rule was right and I did not follow it. Only the first half is a guidance defect.
payload.title: the quality gate says run the repos checks so an agent assembles its own subset

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a dispatch whose recorded spend reaches the session grant ceiling mid-run when the next usage event arrives then the dispatch is stopped on the spend bound rather than running to the wall clock and given a dispatch emitting no events for the configured quiet bound then it is stopped as a runaway and given a lane that is emitting events and inside its budget then it runs past the former 1800s wall clock without being killed and the wall clock remains only as a backstop at a value it does not reach in normal operation with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Split out of `basicly-yvx9` on 2026-08-06 because that bead's acceptance criterion bundled an
independent, cheap fix with this one, which is blocked. `yvx9` keeps the half that needs nothing
new - preserving a killed lane's work - and can ship immediately. This is the structural half.

`yvx9` establishes the defect: terminal authority sits on the one signal that carries no
information about whether work is happening.

| | measures | knows if work is happening | power |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runner_timeout` = 1800s | wall clock since spawn | **no** | **hard kill** |
| `StallWatchdog`, `stall_after` = 900s | commits + dirty tree | yes, partially | flag only |

Measured consequence: the longest *successful* lane ran 1712s, **95.1%** of the cap, and 10 of 68
successes finished past 80% of it. The ceiling sits inside the upper tail of legitimate work.

## Blocked on basicly-rupz, and rupz changes the answer

The obvious fix - make the idle bound terminal - cannot be done with today's probe.
`lane_activity` (supervise.py:2136) hashes `git rev-parse HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain`, so a
lane running a long test suite, or thinking, writes nothing and reads as **idle**. Making that
terminal at 900s would kill a lane running this repo's own gate set. It would trade one wrong kill
for another.

`basicly-rupz` removes that blocker: every metered adapter already emits a per-turn JSONL event
stream that the harness requests, pays for and discards. An event is proof of life whether or not a
file changed.

**And rupz changes what the right bound is, so do not simply implement the idle kill this bead was
first framed as.** Per-turn usage means the D3 spend ceiling can bind *during* a dispatch instead of
only at pass boundaries. Tokens accrue monotonically and are the resource that actually matters,
so a spend bound is strictly better than any clock. The cost of not having it is on the record: a
20,000,000-token grant on `basicly-vhft` overshot to 22,164,783 on 2026-08-06, because
`spend_status` is consulted before a pass and recorded after, with nothing in between.

## What the wall clock becomes

Not removed - **demoted**. A runaway agent looping edit -> test -> edit -> test on one file is
maximally active by every liveness measure; streaming makes it visible without bounding it. So a
terminal bound must remain, and after this bead it is spend plus no-events, with the wall clock
left as a last-resort backstop for the pathological case: a process that hangs holding the pipe, or
a stream that stops while the process does not exit. Set it where it never fires in normal
operation - the 3600s default it was lowered from, or higher.

Do **not** raise `runner_timeout` alone and call this done. That moves the cliff one tail-length out
and weakens the only runaway bound in the process, which is the trap `basicly-vz78`'s missing
forward forecast left behind.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -c "
import json, statistics
d=json.load(open('.basicly/usage/run-records.json'))
ok=[r['duration_s'] for rs in d.values() for r in rs
    if r.get('agent')=='claude' and r.get('outcome')=='executed' and r.get('duration_s')]
print('n', len(ok), 'max', round(max(ok)), 'pct of 1800:', round(max(ok)/1800*100,1))
print('above 80% of cap:', sum(1 for x in ok if x>1440))"
```

Reports the successful-lane tail sitting at 95% of the terminal bound.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

payload.description:
From basicly-u0zg.2 (closed infeasible). GitHub Copilot CLI has NO config-file deny mechanism (deny is --deny-tool CLI-flag-only, session-scoped, never persisted; permissions-config.json stores allows only; github/copilot-cli#2398 unshipped). So the baseline deny-list cannot be projected as managed catalog output for copilot. The only enforcement is invocation-time: extend the copilot runner command template to inject --deny-tool flags derived from permissions.yaml. Belongs at the runner seam (overlaps basicly-45ld). Render-testable via runner dry-run.

Verified 2026-07-18 against copilot CLI v1.0.70: --deny-tool[=tools...] takes copilot-native tool specs and matches shell commands by PREFIX, e.g. --deny-tool='shell(git push --force)' (does not block plain 'git push'); tool names like 'write'. No infix wildcards, so the fine-grained claude glob deny-list maps only PARTIALLY - a documented best-effort projection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- permissions.yaml deny rules gain an optional copilot field of copilot-native --deny-tool specs, authored only for rules copilot can meaningfully express (destructive-rm, force-push, bypass-gates, destructive-git); rules with no faithful copilot form (env-read/env-edit) are omitted with a comment.
- permissions.py exposes the flat de-duplicated copilot deny specs (mirroring claude_deny_patterns).
- The copilot runner command injects one --deny-tool=<spec> per spec, placed after the binary and before -p, populated from the repo permissions.yaml at runner-config load.
- runner dry-run --runner copilot renders the exact argv including the --deny-tool flags; a non-copilot runner is unchanged.
- The prefix-match limitation (variants/flag-reordering not all caught; env rules omitted) is documented where the mapping is authored.
- Deterministic tests cover the spec loader, format_command injection, and the dry-run surface.
payload.title: Guardrails: inject --deny-tool flags on the copilot runner (invocation-time deny)

[merged from basicly-jr0l.30, triage 2026-11-17] Record the mermaid subgraph direction trap in the quirks fragment
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a mermaid subgraph with no edges silently inherits its parent's direction, I want the quirks fragment to name the trap and the fix, so I can avoid rendering columns as reversed horizontal bands.

## Context

Verified against mermaid 11.16.0 on 2026-07-27 while building the readme roadmap: direction inside a subgraph is silently ignored when that subgraph has no edges, so its nodes inherit the parent direction. Four intended columns rendered as four horizontal bands in reverse declaration order, and nothing flagged it because the diagram parsed and rendered. Linking the subgraph containers (p1 ~~~ p2) orders them while preserving the inner direction; linking their nodes across subgraphs does not, and also disables the inner direction. One quirks bullet: trap plus avoidance, plus verify a diagram by rendering it.
Why merged: No mermaid bullet anywhere in .basicly/core or .basicly-local (rg -i mermaid: no hit); one guidance bullet.

[merged from basicly-jr0l.31, triage 2026-11-17] Extend the truncated-output rule to cover a failing command
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a failing command's output is piped through a truncating tool, I want the quality-gate fragment to say to re-run it untruncated before diagnosing, so I can stop losing the diagnostic that explains why it failed.

## Context

The quality-gate fragment says to confirm success from the explicit pass/fail summary line because truncated output can hide a failure, but it is worded only about confirming success. On 2026-07-27 a git push failed with its output piped through tail -5, which discarded the diagnostic; the retry succeeded and the cause is now unknowable. Add the failure direction: when a command fails, re-run it without the truncation before diagnosing, rather than reasoning from the visible tail.
Why merged: Partly delivered: harness-loop references/verification.md 'Read the output and the pass/fail summary, not only the exit code' and references/many-lanes.md:83 'A tail -n of hook output can cut the line ... Capture the run to a file.' The failure-direction sentence is one line.

[merged from basicly-kjc5.49, triage 2026-11-17] Require proving a regression test red when it is written after the fix
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When an agent writes a test after the fix it pins, I want the test-discipline guidance to demand proof that the test fails against the pre-fix code, so I can stop a test that passes for the wrong reason from standing as a regression guard.

## Context

Session retro 2026-07-25. Two concurrency tests written for basicly-kjc5.17 passed with the fix removed - they proved nothing. One used an Event that returns immediately for the thread that set it, so the intended interleaving never happened; the other was accidentally serialized by the GIL because the fake tracker does no IO. Both were caught only because the agent chose to disable the lock and re-run, which nothing asked it to do.

The test-discipline skill says to add the regression test that would have caught the bug first, which assumes test-first ordering and prevents this. In practice a test is often written after the fix, and then passing is not evidence of anything. The missing rule is explicit: when a test is authored after the fix it claims to pin, prove it red against the pre-fix shape - revert the fix, watch it fail for the stated reason, restore. Add the concurrency corollary too, since it bit here: a test cannot prove mutual exclusion by racing, because forcing an interleaving inside the critical section is exactly what the lock prevents and a barrier there deadlocks - assert the contract instead, or use a timed handshake that discriminates in both worlds.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/test-discipline/skill.yaml`
Why merged: Regression-red half delivered: .basicly/core/skills/test-discipline/skill.yaml:28-29 'Watch a regression test fail before the fix' (79072fb9). The mutual-exclusion-without-a-race clause is absent (rg mutual|race|interleav in the skill and references/test-controls.md: no hit). One guidance paragraph.

[merged from basicly-qf98ra9, triage 2026-11-17] Require a documented host behaviour to cite a probe that ran the same command the reader runs
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When an agent documents how a host behaves, I want the claim to cite a probe that ran the exact command the document tells the reader to run, so I can avoid publishing a behaviour measured on a nearby action.

## Evidence

Retro from the handily session 2026-10-13: a probe measured that /reload-plugins does not unload a disabled plugin, and the README then said a reload does not unload an uninstalled plugin. The person's reload did unload it, and a second probe confirmed it (handily-fwkt.10 wrong, handily-fwkt.12 right). The rule 'when two causes predict the same result, change the probe' did not fire because no second cause was seen. Proposed home: validate-as-consumer or the External Facts fragment.
Why merged: One guidance line for validate-as-consumer or External Facts; not present.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a repository that already has basicly runs a standalone kit install, it ends up with two copies of the same kit at two different paths and nothing notices, so an agent may read one and a hook may run the other.

## Measured, 2026-09-12

`basicly install` materialises the catalog and the kit lands at `.basicly/core/kit/<name>/`. A standalone `basicly-<kit> init` vendors to `.basicly/kit/<name>/`. Both are plausible places to look, neither knows about the other, and the two can be at different versions.

Confirmed by running both into throwaway repositories and listing the trees.

## Why it matters more than tidiness

The kit is imported by path. A hook wired against one root keeps running the copy at that root after the other is updated, so an upgrade can appear to have landed and have changed nothing. That is the shape of failure this repository already pays for elsewhere - a stale copy that every diagnostic reports as installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHERE a repository already carries the kit under the basicly-managed root, THE STANDALONE INSTALL SHALL say so and SHALL NOT write a second copy.
- WHERE a repository carries a standalone copy, `basicly install` SHALL report it rather than silently adding a second.
- THE MESSAGE SHALL name both paths and say which one the repository should keep.
- A TEST SHALL create each collision and assert the refusal names both paths.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: install through basicly, then run the standalone init in the same repository, and read what it says
payload.title: two install roots let a repo hold the same kit twice

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a multi lane pass whose lanes each regenerate a shared generated artifact when a landing rebase conflicts only on paths the config declares generated then the merge queue regenerates and continues without spending rework and given a conflict touching any undeclared path then it still bounces to the lane
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-06, landing three lanes from the `basicly-u6jq.1` proof run.
`basicly-l7zo`, `basicly-5xcj` and `basicly-sco6` each edit a different catalog
source - the worktree-isolation skill, the fragments, the python skill - so their
declared scopes are disjoint. Each edit regenerates `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`.

Observed - the first two landed; the third could not:

```
[escalated] build -> build: merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-sco6 onto main
            hit conflicts in: .basicly/generated-manifest.json (rework 2/2)
```

Expected - a pass whose lanes edit different catalog sources does not serialise on the
artifact those edits generate.

## Cause: o8p0's defect class, second variety

`basicly-o8p0` fixed the **append-only** case: `CHANGELOG.md` is written by every lane,
declared by none, and now carried in `[worktree] append_only_paths` so the grouping
contends on it and `preflight` warns. `.basicly/generated-manifest.json` collides the
same way and for the same reason - every lane touches it, no bead declares it - but it
is a **generated artifact**, so the two remedies o8p0 offers are both wrong for it:

- **Serialising** the lanes is unnecessary. The conflict is not semantic; the file is a
  pure function of the tree.
- **Giving one lane the entry** is meaningless. Every lane's edit legitimately changes it.
- **Union merge** would corrupt it outright - it is JSON, not a line-oriented log.

The correct resolution is **regenerate after merge**, which is what unblocked this lane:
`skills-build --all-default-roots` then `build`, so the artifact matches the merged tree
rather than either parent. Picking a side would have left a manifest describing neither.

## Fix shape

- A `[worktree] generated_paths` list (sibling to `append_only_paths`, same authoring
  home) naming artifacts the engine can rebuild. On a rebase conflict confined to those
  paths, the merge queue **regenerates and continues** instead of bouncing to the lane.
  Bounded deliberately: it applies only when every conflicting path is in the list, so a
  genuine source conflict still bounces.
- `preflight` reports it beside the `contend:` line, since the operator can otherwise
  only discover it at the merge queue.

The regeneration command already exists and is already gated - `projection-check` and the
four `projection-*` checks fail when a projected artifact is stale - so a wrong
regeneration cannot pass silently.

## Why this is not just o8p0 again

o8p0's `append_only_paths` is a *contention* declaration: those paths make lanes
serialise. This class wants the opposite treatment - the lanes need not serialise at all,
the artifact simply needs rebuilding once. Folding generated files into
`append_only_paths` would impose a serial chain on every catalog pass for no reason, which
is a throughput cost with no correctness gain.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
payload.title: A generated shared artifact conflicts every multi lane pass and no bead declares it

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07, reading the served board: *"even you mentioned onboarding bootstrap icons and components, i still see a few icons only, and the buttons and components do not look like bootstrap and do not behave like bootstrap."*

And the constraint, in their words: *"you can vendor the bootstrap css, and update the style (css classes) to match our design. i think that bootstrap css can be onboarded using npm as a node package (no CDN, or any internet access for the page to run is allowed)."*

`basicly-e1c4pct` vendored bootstrap **icons** MIT with provenance. Nothing vendored the framework, so every control on the board is hand-rolled CSS: a submit button is a bare `<button>` styled to look like text, and the cards, tables and strips share no component vocabulary.

## Measured

Taken from the served board at 127.0.0.1:8787 on 2026-09-07.

| what a bootstrap page has | what the board has |
| --- | --- |
| `.btn` with size, variant, focus ring and disabled state | a `<button>` with `background: none` and a hover border |
| `.card` with header, body and consistent radius | four different hand-tuned box treatments across regions |
| `.table` with striping and cell padding scale | three tables, each with its own padding literals |
| a spacing scale | ad-hoc px values, ~40 distinct |

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE REPOSITORY SHALL vendor bootstrap's CSS as an npm dependency with its licence and version recorded beside it, as `basicly-e1c4pct` did for the icons.
- WHEN a board page is opened with no network, IT SHALL render fully: no CDN reference, no external font, no remote fetch of any kind.
- WHERE the board draws a control a reader presses, IT SHALL carry bootstrap's button semantics - a visible focus ring, a disabled state, and one size scale.
- THE THREE PAGES - wall, loop and backlog - SHALL share one component vocabulary, so a card on one reads as a card on the others.
- THE PALETTE SHALL stay basicly's own; this record adopts bootstrap's components and spacing scale, not its colours.
- A TEST SHALL assert no page references an external origin, so a CDN cannot be reintroduced silently.

## Scope

- `package.json`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/` (all page templates)
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/vendor/`
- `tests/test_board_offline.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: open each of the three pages with the network disabled and press a control on each

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When basicly worktree merge --mode ci lands a lane, then the full checks ran green on GitHub on the exact tree that main receives and the local run took only the local-only checks.
When two lanes land with --mode ci one after the other, then the second landing is not refused as NOT-READY for an unverified destination.
When main moves by code during the CI wait twice, or the CI run fails, is cancelled or passes only on a rerun, then the landing refuses by name, lands nothing and never force-pushes.
When main receives a CI-proved merge commit, then the quality-gates push run reuses the lane run and its shard jobs log reuse.
payload.description:
## Context
When a lane is ready, I want basicly worktree merge to prove it on GitHub runners instead of a local full verify with a machine-wide quiet window, so a landing costs about 1.5 min of local time instead of about 18 (measured 2026-11-19: ci-weights 17.8 min, ci-revert 18.3 min).

## Design (Orchestrator decisions 2026-11-19 13:28, 13:59 owner go, 15:12 corrections)
--mode ci: preflight as today; rebase; local-only checks (the 9 local_only checks, staged fast checks, tracker write); push the proved head to a new ref land/LANE/N (never force); dispatch quality-gates on it with base = main; wait (first attempt only, 15 min limit); if main moved by ledger commits only, rebase again and land when the tree outside .basicly/ledger equals the proved tree; if main moved by code, one new run, then refuse; merge --no-ff; landing-verification status ci-verified with the run URL and the proved tree, accepted by landing_guard.blocker; push main under the Orchestrator's standing push order; delete land/LANE/N. quality-gates gets a reuse step (actions: read, GH_TOKEN): main's push run skips its checks when the head is the merge commit M or ledger-only commits on it, tree(M) equals tree(M^2), and a first-attempt quality-gates run on M^2 succeeded. Fallback: --mode full stays.

## Links
basicly-svtn4op (CI budget), basicly-br1a0vq (landing lock, lands first). Landing this record's lane moves the local full verify to CI: the exact diff goes to the Orchestrator for the owner's relayed approval before it lands.
payload.title: Prove a landing on GitHub runners instead of a local full verify

payload.text: [conversation 2026-11-19 basicly-ci] Orchestrator decisions: 13:28 UTC design order; 13:59 UTC owner go to the design and a standing push order for landings proved by CI; 15:12 UTC corrections 1 to 7 accepted (new land/ ref per attempt instead of a force-push; tree equality outside the ledger after a second rebase; a ci-verified landing status; ledger-only push reuse; merge --no-ff kept; actions: read and GH_TOKEN for the reuse step; first-attempt runs only). The land/ refs are covered by the Orchestrator's push authority; a classifier refusal of their delete leaves the ref listed for the owner. The landing of this lane needs the owner's relayed approval of the exact diff.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it is not counted as a tool, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Found by the 2026-07-31 session retro while reading `basicly usage report`. The report's Terminal
tools table counts things that are not tools, which undermines its own stated purpose - the skill
uses it to name never-used catalog skills as culling candidates, so noise there can drive a real
culling decision.

**Not a heredoc bug.** `.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py` already tracks heredoc bodies and quote
state (basicly-zcvo). The heredoc-shaped entries (`def` 90, `assert` 83, `PYEOF` 33, `EOF` 28,
`return` 31) all carry `last used` dates of 2026-07-16/17 - they are pre-fix residue, and because
the counter file accumulates by design and is never reset, that residue never ages out.

The live defect is wrapper resolution. Measured on entries last used 2026-07-31 that are not on PATH:

- **Worktree names, 49 counts across 7 entries**: `basicly-kjc5-61` 36, `basicly-jr0l-37` 8,
  `basicly-sy8c` 3, `basicly-2rn9` 1, `basicly-qvd2` 1, `basicly-jr0l-38` 1, `basicly-jr0l-50` 1.
  These come from `uv run --directory <abs-path> <cmd>`: `uv` is in `WRAPPER_TOKENS`, so it unwraps,
  but the flag and its value are not skipped, so the path lands as the head instead of `<cmd>`.
- **`run` 64** - the `uv` subcommand itself surviving as a head rather than resolving to the command
  after it.
- **Shell keywords and functions**: `continue` 9, `break` 6, `write_src` 3 (a function defined and
  called in the same script).

So a session that runs its work through `uv run --directory <worktree>` - which is exactly what this
repo's own multi-lane pattern does - pollutes the table with one entry per worktree, and the real
tool it invoked is never credited.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `uv run --directory <redacted:posix-absolute-path> pytest -q` and then `basicly usage report`.
- Observed: the directory basename is counted as a terminal tool and `pytest` is not credited.
  Expected: `pytest` is credited and the path is not counted.
- Also run a script that defines and calls a shell function, and one containing `continue` or
  `break` inside a loop; observe each counted as a tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the
  tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or
  the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it
  is not counted as a tool, with tests
payload.title: Resolve a wrapped command past its flags so usage counts the real tool

## Context

Split out of basicly-m4zv.13 by owner decision 2026-07-31. That bead delivers the *mechanism*: a phase
may declare a required evidence artifact, and the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and
is non-empty (presence only — the engine never parses it).

It deliberately does not supply a producer, and today there is none. `verify.py` streams each check's
output straight to the terminal uncaptured (that is intentional, so a consumer sees tool output live),
and `rerun_failures(..., capture=True)` captures only on the failure re-run path. So on a **passing**
run nothing is written anywhere, and declaring an evidence artifact for the verify phase would refuse
every advance.

This bead gives verify something to point at, which is what lets this repo dogfood the gate by
declaring it in its own `basicly.toml`.

Design constraints inherited from m4zv.13:

- The engine gates on **presence only**; the producer owns the content. Do not add parsing.
- Live terminal output must not regress — a consumer watching a run still sees each tool's own output.
- Deterministic: no model involvement, no judged content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a passing verify run when it completes then a non-empty run artifact exists at a stable declared path and the live terminal output of each check is unchanged, so the evidence gate from basicly-m4zv.13 can be declared for the verify phase in this repo and passes

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.description:
Filed 2026-08-09 from a defect this session actually committed, at the owner's direction.

## What happened

A 15-file catalog edit was written as:

    MOVE="tool-ast-grep tool-curl ... tool-yq"
    for s in $MOVE; do ...; done

zsh does not word-split an unquoted scalar, so the loop ran ONCE with the whole 260-character
string as $s, touched nothing, and exited 0. The only reason it was visible is that the loop
body carried a `grep -q ... || { echo MISS; continue; }` guard, which printed one line. Without
that guard it reads as complete success and 15 files silently stay as they were.

## Why guidance did not prevent it

The rule already exists and is ALWAYS-ON. `.basicly/core/fragments/tools/
non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml` says verbatim: "Never loop over an unquoted variable
(`for x in $LIST`): zsh does not word-split, so it runs once with the whole string and the
silent no-op looks like success." It was projected into CLAUDE.md and in context from the first
token of the session. It did not bind.

This is not a discovery failure, so the two cheapest remedies are both refuted:

- Routing a tool skill would not have helped: `tool-zsh` has been `invocation: user` since
  before this session, because its content was already PROMOTED into the always-on fragment.
  That promotion is the fix that was already tried.
- Adding more always-on text is the one remedy with evidence against it. The always-on baseline
  is at cap and the open question recorded against it is adherence, not size.

What is left is a deterministic gate, which is this repo's stated doctrine for exactly this:
guidance that must bind becomes a hook.

## Why the matcher can be tight AND complete

Shell state does not persist between Bash tool calls in this harness, so the only reachable
form of the defect is an assignment and its loop in the SAME command. That means matching a
scalar assignment whose value contains whitespace, plus a `for X in $NAME` over that same name,
catches every instance that can occur here while firing on nothing else.

Deliberately NOT matched, each because it is correct or ambiguous:

- `for x in "\${arr[@]}"` - the correct form.
- `for x in a b c` - an inline list.
- `for x in $arr` where arr is an array - zsh DOES split an array; only scalars are the trap.
- `for x in $(cmd)` - also unsplit in zsh, but idiomatic and often intended; blocking it would
  make the gate cry wolf, and a gate that cries wolf gets switched off.
- a name assigned with no whitespace in its value - the loop correctly runs once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a Bash tool call assigns a whitespace-containing scalar and then loops over it unquoted
  in the same command, the hook shall exit 2 and name both the variable and the corrected form.
- When a Bash tool call loops over an array, an inline list, or a quoted array expansion, the
  hook shall exit 0 and write nothing.
- Where the payload is malformed, absent, or not a Bash call, the hook shall exit 0, so a bug
  in the guard can never lock an agent out of running commands.
- The hook shall be declared in the catalog hook manifest for the claude manager at the
  pretooluse stage with a Bash matcher, and shall be projected into .claude/settings.json.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/unsplit-loop-guard.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/tools/non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_unsplit_loop_guard.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Bash call containing `V="a b c"` and `for x in $V; do echo $x; done` under zsh.
2. Observe one line of output containing 'a b c', not three lines.
3. Observe exit code 0.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_git_hooks/test_unsplit_loop_guard.py -q` passes, and piping the
recorded payload of this session's own failing command into the hook exits 2 naming MOVE.
payload.title: Refuse a for-loop over an unsplit scalar before it runs

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-09-01 during a live supervised pass on basicly-atrqcd. A commit staging the ledger was refused:

```text
spend-accuracy: basicly-rv7q88: basicly-rv7q88 spent 1,025,735 tokens against a
  recorded forecast of 11,610,753 (0.088x), outside the 10x band
```

At that moment `basicly-rv7q88` was in phase `build` with exactly 1,025,735 tokens on the live board. The gate compared a lane that had not finished against the forecast for the whole lane, and named the estimator as the fault.

`decompose.spend_accuracy` filters the dispatch population four ways and none of them is about completion. It drops an entry that is not a write phase, one whose tokens are unmetered or estimated, one whose outcome is `FAILED`, and one whose forecast was a stand-in. A dispatch entry for a bead whose lane is still open passes every one of those and is folded as though the work were done.

The remedy the gate prints is to freeze the record or fix the estimator. Both are wrong here: freezing banks a partial measurement as history, and the estimator is not what produced 0.088x.

The failure mode is that any commit taken while a pass runs can be refused by a lane that is merely early, and the operator is invited to bank a false number to get past it. The supervisor own tracker-state commit is exposed to the same refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a bead has a dispatch entry but its own work has not finished, THE GATE SHALL NOT score it.
- WHEN the bead finishes, ITS folded actual SHALL enter the population unchanged.
- WHEN the gate excludes a bead for being unfinished, ITS summary SHALL count it, so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
- WHEN the population is empty of finished beads, THE GATE SHALL report that rather than passing quietly.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `.scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py`
- `tests/test_spend_calibration.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 by running a freshly installed codex CLI against this repo's own projected
skills. Codex refuses to load three of them:

    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-fzf/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-git-delta/SKILL.md: missing field `description`

This is a regression inside the unreleased set, not a pre-existing wart. At v0.5.1
`tool-bat/SKILL.md` carried a description; on main it does not, because basicly-m4zv.1 makes
a user-invoked entry project no `description` line. Claude tolerates the omission - that
tolerance is what basicly-m4zv.7 had to fix when the generated marker leaked into the
description slot - but codex treats description as required and hard-errors, so the skill
simply does not exist for a codex consumer.

The design tension is real rather than a coding slip. The invocation axis says a user-invoked
entry carries no description because nothing can route to it, so a description is context
load bought for no reach. Codex's loader makes "user-invoked" unrepresentable: an entry either
carries a description or fails to load. This is the same shape as the model-id problem - a
portable catalog concept one family cannot express - and it wants the same kind of answer, a
per-family projection rule rather than a change to the portable concept.

Two candidate stances, to be decided in the work: project a description for user-invoked
entries on families whose loader requires one, or omit the entry entirely for those families
rather than emitting a file that cannot load. Silently shipping an unloadable file is the one
option to rule out.

Blocks the release: v0.6.0 would otherwise ship a change that removes three skills from every
codex consumer without saying so.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run any codex command in this repo, e.g. `codex exec --json -s read-only "reply with
  exactly: ok" < <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`, and read stderr.
- Observed: three `failed to load skill ... missing field description` errors for the
  user-invoked skills tool-bat, tool-fzf and tool-git-delta.
- Compare `git show v0.5.1:.agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md` (has a description) against the
  file on main (has none).
- Expected: every projected skill loads on every agent family the projection targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader
  requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given
  the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it
  rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load,
  with tests
payload.title: User-invoked skills fail to load on codex because they carry no description

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-30 while verifying a competitive claim from the `oh-my-agent` analysis
(`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`), and it turns out to be a hole in our own gate.

The repo's positioning - now in `README.md`, `site/index.html` and the GitHub About - claims
enforcement at **commit time** as the thing that distinguishes us from a projector whose drift
check is CI-only. On the specific axis of *projection staleness* that claim is currently false.

What actually runs locally:

- `protect-generated-commit` compares each **staged generated blob** against the hash in
  `generated-manifest.json`. Its docstring is precise about the case it covers: a hand-edit that
  skips the rebuild. It cannot see a stale projection, because a fragment edit does not stage the
  generated file at all - the output on disk still matches the manifest.
- `pre-commit-script` runs `[[verify.checks]]` mode `fast`: ruff, ruff-format, pyright, bandit,
  lint-imports.
- `pre-push-script` runs mode `full`: the above plus pytest.

`basicly check` appears in **none** of them. Nor do `skills-check`, `agents-check` or
`hooks-check`. They run in one CI job. `tests/test_docs_drift.py` is docs-to-code drift, not
projection drift, so pytest at pre-push does not cover it either.

So: edit a fragment, never rebuild, commit, push. Nothing local objects. The projection is stale
in the tree and on the remote until CI says so - which is exactly the posture we describe as the
competitor's weakness.

The fix is to add the four projection gates to the locally-run verify modes. They are the gates
`CLAUDE.md` already names as the projection gates, so this is wiring an existing check into the
stage that was supposed to run it, not new enforcement.

Open question this bead must settle rather than assume: whether they belong in `fast` (every
commit) or only `full` (pre-push). `fast` is the stronger guarantee and matches the published
claim; the cost is four extra subprocesses on every commit, and `skills-check
--all-default-roots` is the slowest of them. Measure before choosing, and if the answer is `full`,
then the published wording must say pre-push rather than commit time - correcting the claim is an
acceptable outcome of this bead, silently leaving it overstated is not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Edit any fragment body under `.basicly/core/fragments/`.
2. Do not run `basicly build`.
3. `git add` the fragment and commit, then push.
4. Observed: every hook passes; the generated instruction files are stale in the tree and on the
   remote, and only CI reports it. Expected: a local gate refuses the commit or the push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a fragment edited without a rebuild when the local git hooks run then a projection gate fails before the change can reach the remote, and the positioning wording in README site and repo About names the stage that actually enforces it
payload.title: No local gate catches a stale projection so the commit-time claim is overstated

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root
payload.description:
## Context

Surfaced by the 2026-07-30 `oh-my-agent` analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`) and
confirmed against our source and against pathlib's actual behaviour.

`planner.py` builds every projection output path by joining catalog-supplied strings onto the repo
root, with no containment check:

- `output_path=repo_root / output.path` (`src/basicly/planner.py:31`)
- `output_path = repo_root / output.path_template.format(fragment_id=fragment.id)`
  (`src/basicly/planner.py:39`)

Neither input is constrained. A schema audit found `pattern` on exactly two fields in the whole
catalog - `block.schema.json` `.properties.id` and `agent.schema.json` `.properties.name` - so a
fragment `id` and a target `path`/`path_template` are free-form strings.

Two distinct escapes, and the first is the nastier because it is silent:

1. **An absolute `path` replaces the root outright.** `Path('<redacted:posix-home-path>') / '<redacted:posix-absolute-path>'` is
   `<redacted:posix-absolute-path>` - pathlib discards the left operand. There is no traversal sequence to spot in a
   review; the string just looks like a path.
2. **A traversal sequence escapes upward.** `repo_root / '../../etc/passwd'` resolves outside the
   repo, and a `fragment_id` containing `../` reaches the same place through the `path_template`
   branch.

## Severity, stated honestly

**Not remote code execution and not a high-severity issue.** The inputs come from the catalog: our
own `.basicly/core/targets/` and the consumer's `.basicly-local/` overlay. Writing them is already
writing to the repo. So the realistic threat is a **third-party or copied overlay** a consumer
installs without auditing, and the realistic damage is `basicly build` writing a generated file
outside the repo - which is exactly the class of uninvited write `tracker_usage.is_enabled` was
already hardened against for a different reason.

It is worth fixing anyway on the repo's own rule - validate external input at trust boundaries -
and because the fix is small and the failure mode is silent. An overlay is a trust boundary the
moment it can come from somewhere else.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In `.basicly-local/`, declare a target output whose `path` is an absolute path outside the repo
   (or a `path_template` plus a fragment whose `id` contains `../`).
2. Run `basicly build`.
3. Observed: the projection writes outside the repo root, and the manifest records it. Expected:
   the build refuses the declaration and names the offending field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root, or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence, when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value, and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root
payload.title: Refuse a catalog path that escapes the repo root when planning the projection

payload.text: [harness-info] Review evidence 2026-07-30 at 2a0ba60: the escape is worse than filed - the write happens before any check would notice it. cli.py:304 write_if_changed(item.output_path) runs before the relative_to(repo_root) at cli.py:307 that would raise, so a hostile catalog gets one arbitrary file write per output before the crash. The refusal therefore belongs at plan time in planner.py (both join sites, planner.py:31 and :39), not in the render loop.

payload.description:
## Context

From the Archon analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/archon.md`). Its `evidence_policy.required`
plus typed node artifacts refuses terminal success unless a declared evidence file exists on disk -
the engine gating on **presence only**, the workflow producing the content. Their formulation is the
clearest statement of our own split: *"code computes, YAML coordinates"* (`schemas/workflow.ts:105`).

This plugs a hole we have. A lane can reach ship having recorded a passing verify gate with nothing
to point at: the gate records a status, not an artifact. When a landing is later questioned - a
forecast miss, a coupling dispute, a rework argument - the evidence is whatever happened to be
committed, which is exactly the situation the `[harness-*]` marker families were introduced to fix
for cost and decisions but never for verification output.

Presence-only is the important constraint and the reason this is cheap: the engine must not parse or
judge the artifact, only assert it exists and is non-empty, so it adds no nondeterminism and needs no
schema per artifact type. That keeps it on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.

Note the accompanying reject, worth recording next to it: Archon's own completion gate is
`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete` (`dag-executor.ts:4602`), which lets a model's
self-emitted `<promise>DONE</promise>` short-circuit the deterministic check entirely. Adopt the
evidence requirement; reject the disjunction.

Open question this bead must settle: which phases owe an artifact, and whether a missing one blocks
or is recorded. Blocking every phase is likely too strict at first; verify is the phase where the
argument is strongest, because a verify gate with no output is the case that has actually caused
disputes here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a phase that declares a required evidence artifact when the loop attempts to advance past it then the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and is non-empty, the engine never parses or judges the content, and the artifact path is recorded on the bead
payload.title: Require a declared evidence artifact before a phase can report success

payload.text:
Owner decision 2026-07-31 — the open question is settled: **opt-in declaration, blocking where declared.**

- A phase may *declare* a required evidence artifact path. When one is declared, the advance past that
  phase is refused unless the path exists and is non-empty. Presence only — the engine never parses or
  judges the content, so it stays on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.
- Nothing is declared by default, so there is zero behaviour change for existing consumers and the
  change is reversible. Blocking every phase was rejected as too strict; record-only was rejected as
  toothless (it reduces to a log line and would not have prevented the disputes this bead was filed
  about).
- The artifact path is recorded on the bead.

Scope boundary found while deciding: `verify.py` streams check output straight to the terminal and
captures nothing on a passing run, so **no artifact file exists for verify today**. Declaring one
therefore needs a producer. That is deliberately NOT in this bead — it is filed separately, so this
bead delivers the mechanism only and cannot destabilise the landing path before the u6jq.1 proof run.

Archon's own completion gate (`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete`) stays rejected:
adopt the evidence requirement, never the disjunction that lets a self-emitted signal short-circuit it.
